"That's why I come back to the fact that this is an international conflict," he said, adding that "immediate action is required."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Albania rioters clash with police for Socialist government as European unrest spreads
summary: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama vowed not to resign as protests in Tirana erupted for a third day, with police deploying tear gas and water cannons.
story: Clashes between police and protesters who are against Albania's Socialist government erupted in the country's capital of Tirana for the third consecutive day on Thursday. (Credit: Reuters)

Clashes between police and protesters who are against Albania's Socialist government erupted in the country's capital for the third consecutive day Thursday as Prime Minister Edi Rama vowed he will not resign.

Rioters in Tirana were seen throwing rocks at a police cordon outside Albania's Education Ministry, prompting law enforcement to respond with tear gas and water cannons, according to The Associated Press.
The clashes followed riots on Wednesday when protesters attacked government buildings, banks and businesses, leaving 89 people injured, including 61 police officers.
"As for calls for my resignation, governments are changed through democratic elections. We had elections last year, not a revolution," Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama told Reuters on Thursday.
ALBANIAN PROTESTERS FLOOD STREETS DEMANDING PRIME MINISTER'S RESIGNATION AMID CORRUPTION ACCUSATIONS
Riot police officers detain a hooded protester during clashes near the Ministry of Education in Tirana, Albania, on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026. (Hameraldi Agolli/AP)

"My responsibility is to listen, address legitimate concerns and keep Albania moving forward," he added. "The alternative would be a betrayal of the Albanians who gave me a strong mandate to complete negotiations on European Union membership."

Thursday's protests included student groups seeking education reforms, as well as others staging a broader anti-government movement opposed to a major development project linked to President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, the AP reported.
A protester pushes a riot police officer's shield during an anti-government demonstration in Tirana, Albania, on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. (Hameraldi Agolli/AP)
The so-called flamingo movement is calling for the resignation of Rama over allegations of widespread corruption. The movement earned the name after protesters used signs depicting the pink bird.

"The message from the streets is clear: Albanians have had enough. Public patience with Edi Rama’s socialist government has come to an end," Agim Nesho, former Albanian ambassador to the United States, told Fox News Digital on Thursday.

"The wheels are coming off Edi Rama’s socialist government. After 13 years in power, his administration faces mounting accusations of corruption, misuse of public funds, and political favoritism," Nesho said. "Meanwhile, poverty, unemployment, inadequate public services, and the mass exodus of young Albanians seeking better opportunities in Europe have fueled widespread anger. Critics argue that, as with other failed socialist governments, the political elite has benefited while ordinary citizens have been left struggling to make ends meet."
An EU delegation in Albania called late Wednesday for a proportionate response from authorities, expressing concern at "the violent escalation at the protest in Tirana."
JARED KUSHNER'S OVERSEAS LUXURY RESORT PROJECT FACES ANTI-CORRUPTION INVESTIGATION DURING VIOLENT PROTESTS
Protesters set fire to a barricade during clashes near the Education Ministry in Tirana, Albania, on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026. (Hameraldi Agolli/AP)
Rama won his fourth term as prime minister last year, running on a platform centered around Albania joining the EU, which it hopes to achieve as early as 2028, according to Reuters.
Student organizers told Reuters that the protests are over higher education costs, a lack of financial support, conditions at universities and job prospects after graduating.

The prime minister said to the news agency that he is ready to discuss the cost of education, but added, "Attacking institutions, destroying public property and threatening public safety have nothing to do with the legitimate demands of students."
Hooded protesters smash a storefront window during clashes in Tirana, Albania, on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. (Hameraldi Agolli/AP)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Corruption must be confronted and, as the EU itself has recently reaffirmed, Albania is tackling it as never before," Rama also said. "Perhaps some forces, at home and abroad, do not want Albania to succeed as a forerunner for EU membership. But I will not allow violence to derail Albania's European future."
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Russians locked out of bank accounts and apartments as Ukraine hits data centers
summary: From accessing their money to ordering a taxi or takeout — millions of Russians were feeling the impact of Ukrainian strikes on the data centers of the country’s internet giant Yandex in their daily life.
story: From accessing their money to ordering a taxi or takeout — millions of Russians were feeling the impact of Ukrainian strikes on the data centers of the country’s internet giant Yandex in their daily life.

“I ended up in a situation where I had absolutely no money. Well, I had the money, but it was inaccessible,” said Irina, a blogger from St. Petersburg, who had not been able to access her money for four days when she spoke with NBC News last week.

Irina, who like several other interviewees did not want her last name shared while speaking with a foreign news organization on a sensitive matter, said her rent was due the day the first outages happened, when she hoped “that it would be fixed in a few hours.” Days later, she still had no access to money to pay for utilities or even food for her small child.
The strikes that took place over several days earlier this month were the first publicized attacks on Russian data centers as Ukraine seeks to bring the war home for Russians.

The disruption hit a myriad of services provided by Yandex, a tech giant akin to Google whose services are deeply integrated into daily life in Russia, and whose digital infrastructure is relied on by other third-party platforms.

Many people took to social media to complain about not being able to order a taxi or food delivery. Others reported not being able to access their files on the company’s storage service, while some even struggled to get into their homes after their digital keys went offline.

title: Ukraine claims world’s first drone evacuation of wounded soldier
summary: Ukraine has shared a video showing what it says is the world’s first evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontlines by drone.
story: Ukraine has shared a video showing what it says is the world’s first evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontlines by drone.
The “historic” mission comes just as Kyiv faces a dire turn in its relationship with Washington over the withdrawal of support in its fight against Russia.

Shared by the 92nd Separate Assault Brigade on Monday, the video shows the soldier strapping himself into a large drone and being flown at what appears to be relatively low altitude over blurred-out territory. The drone carefully lowers him down and the drone operator greets him with “Welcome back to the ground!” The video also showed blurred faces of drone operators who carried out the mission.

The post said the unidentified infantryman was wounded while at his position. “Due to intense enemy drone activity and the presence of landmines, evacuation using conventional unmanned ground vehicles was impossible,” the brigade said.
Injured Ukrainian soldier rescued with a drone
“At that point, the specialists in our unit took it upon themselves to attempt something that had never been done before: evacuating a serviceman using an aerial drone,” it added.
The craft used was a heavy-lift hexacopter, it said, originally designed as a bomber by a Ukrainian manufacturer. It looks about twice the size of the soldier in the video.
The specialists working on the mission had to ensure the drone could carry a human being without flipping over or swaying excessively, according to the unit.

The rescued soldier is currently undergoing treatment and rehabilitation, the brigade added. The squad leader and programmer with the brigade, only identified by his call sign Napalm, called the soldier a “hero” for agreeing to the mission, “having seen and heard the kind of machine that had arrived to get him.”
In a separate statement, Ukraine’s Ground Forces said its drone units are already conducting operations “that were recently considered science fiction.”
The war has increasingly become a technological arms race, with both Ukraine and Russia relying on drones to reduce human casualties.

The conflict has taken a severe toll on both armies, although neither side reports up-to-date numbers of those killed, injured or missing. Ukraine in particular has faced a severe shortage of manpower as it has tried to ramp up recruitment.

Ukraine had a major leap in drone technology this year, allowing it to limit Russian logistics in occupied territories as well as strike deeper inside Russia to target Russian oil refineries, commercial warehouses and data centers.
“This mission proves once again that Ukrainian service members, working in tandem with Ukrainian manufacturers, are setting global trends in the conduct of warfare,” the brigade’s statement added.

Despite hoping that its drone innovation would give it the upper hand at the negotiating table, Kyiv has faced pressure from the U.S. to halt its strikes on Russian oil sites after President Donald Trump signed a diesel deal with the Kremlin earlier this month.
Kyiv has since also reported gaps in intelligence sharing and restrictions on Elon Musk’s Starlink service that is crucial for its drone missions, battlefield communications and air defense.

The drone evacuation comes just days after Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced the Ukrainian government had approved an “experimental project” to use drones for medical logistics. Koretskyi said flights would require coordination with the military, and drones would be given a special status and would be identifiable in the air.

“During the war, moving medical cargo by road can cost critical time, especially for transplants,” he said. “Drones will be able to carry medicines, medical products, blood samples, and donor organs between hospitals, including from remote areas.”

title: Dramatic images show violent unrest sweeping across France
summary: France unrest protest photos over the weekend Macron election buildup
story: Widespread violence erupted across France over the weekend, as rioters and looters ransacked storefronts, clashed with police and set fire to municipal buildings.
Nearly 2,400 people were arrested and almost 1,000 police officers and firefighters were injured, the French Interior Ministry said, after some of the worst unrest the country has seen in years.

title: CNN’s Christiane Amanpour to depart from network after 43 years
summary: Christiane Amanpour, CNN’s chief international anchor and a fixture of the 24/7 news network for more than four decades, plans to leave the company next June.
story: Christiane Amanpour, CNN’s chief international anchor and a fixture of the 24/7 news network for more than four decades, plans to leave the company next June.

“After more than 43 years at CNN, Christiane has decided that the time is right to begin a new chapter,” Mark Thompson, CNN’s chief executive, said in a letter to newsroom employees that was obtained by NBC News.

Thompson said Amanpour, 68, plans to “scale back” her eponymous CNN International show to once a week early in 2027. “The program will conclude in May,” Thompson added, “and she will leave CNN at the end of June.”

“Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months,” Thompson said. “Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but l’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally.”

Amanpour has covered nearly every major international conflict and global crisis of the last four decades, including the fall of the Berlin Wall, the Bosnian War, the Persian Gulf War, the post-9/11 U.S. wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, the Arab Spring, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and Israel’s war in Gaza.

She has also interviewed world leaders, including former President Bill Clinton, former British Prime Minister Tony Blair, former Libyan strongman Moammar Gadhafi, and various Iranian presidents, including Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Hassan Rouhani.
For Subscribers

In a statement, Amanpour confirmed her departures from both CNN and PBS, where she hosts the talk show “Amanpour & Company.” She also thanked “the amazingly talented people I’ve worked with throughout this incredible journey,” especially her “beloved show teams and field crews.”
For Subscribers
“We together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and the humanity, so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world, without fear nor favor,” Amanpour said in part.
Amanpour’s exit comes just weeks after David Ellison’s media corporation Paramount Skydance formally took over Warner Bros. Discovery, the parent company of CNN.
Thompson will remain the head of CNN under the brand’s new ownership, reporting directly to Skydance co-CEOs Ellison and Ynon Kreiz.

title: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts likely out for season after blood clots found in lungs and leg
summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs and leg, the team said Monday, likely sidelining the Super Bowl MVP for the rest of 2026.
story: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs and leg, the team said Monday, likely sidelining the Super Bowl MVP for the rest of 2026.
Hurts last played Oct. 11, in the Eagles’ 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London before he was kept off the field in Sunday’s 25-14 setback  to the visiting Carolina Panthers.
Hurts was originally diagnosed with “superficial vein thrombosis” in his left calf, the team said.

“After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli,” the statement continued. “He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations.”
Both deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) are forms of venous thromboembolism, commonly known as blood clots in the veins, according to the Centers for Disease Control.

DVT is when a blood clot develops in a vein deep within the body, most commonly in the leg, the CDC says. PE happens when pieces of a blood clot from a DVT break off and travel to the veins in the lungs.
The clots can prevent blood from reaching the lungs, which can be fatal.
More Sports from NBC News

This Paralympian has two goals: Win medals and give away $500,000 to her teammates‘Swagger on a trillion’: The booming business of styling NFL playersThis Super Bowl contender has an elite offense and defense — and one potentially fatal flaw
This Paralympian has two goals: Win medals and give away $500,000 to her teammates

This Super Bowl contender has an elite offense and defense — and one potentially fatal flaw
He’s being treated with blood thinners and “during this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football,” according to the Eagles.
Hurts was held out of the game on Sunday after the Eagles announced last week a superficial blood clot was found in London ahead of the game against the Jaguars.
Despite that diagnosis, Hurts still played the full game in London.

“Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that [Hurts] could safely play,” the team said last week, adding that Hurts “played without limitation.”

But when a follow-up scan was conducted back in Philadelphia, the team said the superficial blood clot had moved, which prompted them to pull Hurts from the game against the Panthers. Further testing revealed the deep vein clot and the clots in the lungs, leading to Hurts being indefinitely sidelined.
For Subscribers
The team didn’t set an exact timeline for his return, though action for 2026 seems highly unlikely.
For Subscribers

A blood thinner treatment can typically last between three months and six months as doctors bring the condition under control and search for any previously undiagnosed, underlying conditions in a patient.
And contact sport athletes cannot play while taking blood thinner due to the risk of an uncontrollable, and potentially deadly, bleed from an injury.
“We anticipate that he will have no long-term effect,” the club said.
Hurts was MVP of Super Bowl 59, leading his team to a 40-22 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Feb. 9 2025, in New Orleans.
The team’s 2026 fortunes now rest in the hands of career backup Tanner McKee, a sixth-round 2023 pick.

The 26-year-old Stanford alum comes from the same high school graduation class as current NFL signal callers Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers, Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Will Levis, who is on the practice squad of the New York Jets.

Philadelphia won the 2018 Super Bowl with backup QB Nick Foles leading the Birds past Tom Brady’s New England Patriots. The journeyman Foles was the game’s MVP,  executing one of football’s most famous trick plays that evening, the “Philly Special.”

title: Supreme Court rejects alleged 9/11 mastermind’s attempt to revive plea deal
summary: The Supreme Court rejected an appeal brought by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and two other alleged 9/11 plotters seeking to hold the government to a plea deal.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal brought by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and two other alleged 9/11 plotters seeking to hold the government to a plea deal it later withdrew.

The court action removes one barrier to Mohammed standing trial before a military commission in 2028, where the death penalty is a possible punishment. He has been held at the U.S. base in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, since 2006.

Mohammed is accused of being the ringleader of the plot to crash hijacked planes into the World Trade Center in New York and the Pentagon on Sept. 11, 2001. A fourth plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania.
The other two men who appealed to the Supreme Court were Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi and Walid bin Attash, who are also held at Guantanamo and set to face trial.
The three men had agreed to a plea deal with military prosecutors in 2024, signed off on by a military commission judge, that would have given them life sentences.
But days later, then-Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin rejected the proposal, saying he had the authority to override the deal.
For Subscribers

Military courts said he had no such authority but, in an August ruling, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit ruled in favor of the government, prompting the men to appeal to the Supreme Court.
For Subscribers
They argued, among other things, that the appeals court had no authority to intervene in the case.
The long delay in Mohammed facing trial was caused partly by concerns about evidence obtained via CIA torture.
A fourth alleged plotter earmarked for trial, Ali Abdul Aziz Ali, was not involved in the appeal.

title: CNN’s Christiane Amanpour to depart from network after 43 years
summary: Christiane Amanpour, CNN’s chief international anchor and a fixture of the 24/7 news network for more than four decades, plans to leave the company next June.
story: Christiane Amanpour, CNN’s chief international anchor and a fixture of the 24/7 news network for more than four decades, plans to leave the company next June.

“After more than 43 years at CNN, Christiane has decided that the time is right to begin a new chapter,” Mark Thompson, CNN’s chief executive, said in a letter to newsroom employees that was obtained by NBC News.

Thompson said Amanpour, 68, plans to “scale back” her eponymous CNN International show to once a week early in 2027. “The program will conclude in May,” Thompson added, “and she will leave CNN at the end of June.”

“Christiane has thought carefully about this decision, and she and I have been discussing it for some months,” Thompson said. “Like so many CNNers who will hear the news today, I’m very sorry to see her go, but l’ve come to accept that this is the right time for her, both personally and professionally.”

Amanpour has covered nearly every major international conflict and global crisis of the last four decades, including the fall of the Berlin Wall, the Bosnian War, the Persian Gulf War, the post-9/11 U.S. wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, the Arab Spring, Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and Israel’s war in Gaza.

She has also interviewed world leaders, including former President Bill Clinton, former British Prime Minister Tony Blair, former Libyan strongman Moammar Gadhafi, and various Iranian presidents, including Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Hassan Rouhani.
For Subscribers

In a statement, Amanpour confirmed her departures from both CNN and PBS, where she hosts the talk show “Amanpour & Company.” She also thanked “the amazingly talented people I’ve worked with throughout this incredible journey,” especially her “beloved show teams and field crews.”
For Subscribers
“We together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and the humanity, so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world, without fear nor favor,” Amanpour said in part.
Amanpour’s exit comes just weeks after David Ellison’s media corporation Paramount Skydance formally took over Warner Bros. Discovery, the parent company of CNN.
Thompson will remain the head of CNN under the brand’s new ownership, reporting directly to Skydance co-CEOs Ellison and Ynon Kreiz.

title: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts likely out for season after blood clots found in lungs and leg
summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs and leg, the team said Monday, likely sidelining the Super Bowl MVP for the rest of 2026.
story: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs and leg, the team said Monday, likely sidelining the Super Bowl MVP for the rest of 2026.
Hurts last played Oct. 11, in the Eagles’ 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London before he was kept off the field in Sunday’s 25-14 setback  to the visiting Carolina Panthers.
Hurts was originally diagnosed with “superficial vein thrombosis” in his left calf, the team said.

“After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli,” the statement continued. “He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations.”
Both deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) are forms of venous thromboembolism, commonly known as blood clots in the veins, according to the Centers for Disease Control.

DVT is when a blood clot develops in a vein deep within the body, most commonly in the leg, the CDC says. PE happens when pieces of a blood clot from a DVT break off and travel to the veins in the lungs.
The clots can prevent blood from reaching the lungs, which can be fatal.

He’s being treated with blood thinners and “during this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football,” according to the Eagles.
Hurts was held out of the game on Sunday after the Eagles announced last week a superficial blood clot was found in London ahead of the game against the Jaguars.
Despite that diagnosis, Hurts still played the full game in London.

“Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that [Hurts] could safely play,” the team said last week, adding that Hurts “played without limitation.”

But when a follow-up scan was conducted back in Philadelphia, the team said the superficial blood clot had moved, which prompted them to pull Hurts from the game against the Panthers. Further testing revealed the deep vein clot and the clots in the lungs, leading to Hurts being indefinitely sidelined.
For Subscribers
The team didn’t set an exact timeline for his return, though action for 2026 seems highly unlikely.
For Subscribers

A blood thinner treatment can typically last between three months and six months as doctors bring the condition under control and search for any previously undiagnosed, underlying conditions in a patient.
And contact sport athletes cannot play while taking blood thinner due to the risk of an uncontrollable, and potentially deadly, bleed from an injury.
“We anticipate that he will have no long-term effect,” the club said.
Hurts was MVP of Super Bowl 59, leading his team to a 40-22 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Feb. 9 2025, in New Orleans.
The team’s 2026 fortunes now rest in the hands of career backup Tanner McKee, a sixth-round 2023 pick.

The 26-year-old Stanford alum comes from the same high school graduation class as current NFL signal callers Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers, Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Will Levis, who is on the practice squad of the New York Jets.

Philadelphia won the 2018 Super Bowl with backup QB Nick Foles leading the Birds past Tom Brady’s New England Patriots. The journeyman Foles was the game’s MVP,  executing one of football’s most famous trick plays that evening, the “Philly Special.”

title: Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie
summary: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up.
story: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up.
“Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk posted on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.”

One SpaceX share is currently valued at about $150. With approximately 72 million children under the age of 18 in the U.S., Musk’s donation would currently be worth about $10.8 billion — less than 2% of his current net worth. He provided no additional information. Musk could not be reached for additional comment.

His statement comes one day after officials at Anthropic said the company would commit 5% of company shares to a “public benefit fund” in order to address “labor market impacts” of AI.In a statement, Anthropic officials said the fund could make charitable donations or direct money to “specific populations,” emphasizing the fund’s “versatility.”

“Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” they said. Anthropic has been preparing for an initial public offering — releasing its stock for trading on public markets — that analysts say would value the company at more than $1 trillion. The company has long championed employees’ charitable giving by promising to match their donations.
Musk replied to Anthropic on X saying it should give shares “directly to the public.”

While evidence of AI’s impact on work so far remains mixed, a core premise underlying the current artificial intelligence investment boom is that it will make business processes vastly more efficient, including by eroding returns to human labor. That’s prompted fears about exacerbating income inequality and sparked worries of a “permanent underclass” forming throughout society. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has been at the forefront of such warnings, predicting that 50% of all white-collar work could be eliminated by AI before the end of the decade.

An Associated Press poll published last week found 64% of U.S. adults believe AI is developing “too fast,” with 8 in 10 saying the government should prioritize protecting the country’s workforce. A separate NBC News survey published last month found 70% of Americans are more worried than excited about AI, with a majority stating they would oppose construction of a data center in their neighborhood.
How data centers globally have become military targets

Notably, even before the advent of current advanced AI models, labor’s share of economic growth had been seeing precipitous declines. The Trump administration has sought to bridge some of that gap by seeding financial accounts for children born starting in 2025 with $1,000. Other high-profile business people have pledged additional amounts to the accounts, including SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell, who along with her husband planned to give money to 2 million children in low-income areas, especially in Texas.

Musk has made numerous bold statements in his career only to subsequently not follow through on them. Among the most high-profile was his August 2018 announcement that he had “secured” funding to take Tesla private. The transaction failed to materialize and cost Musk his chairmanship of Tesla.

title: Supreme Court to hear a new case on race and school admissions, this time in Maryland
summary: The Supreme Court agreed to hear a new challenge to school admissions policies on diversity, taking up a case on magnet programs in Montgomery County, Maryland.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear a new challenge to school admissions policies aimed at fostering diversity, taking up a case targeting a lottery-based process for magnet programs in a Maryland county.

The court agreed to take up an appeal brought by the Association for Education Fairness seeking to revive a lawsuit it filed against the Montgomery County Board of Education. Montgomery County is a large and diverse county in the suburbs of Washington, D.C.

The challengers argue that a policy in Montgomery County's STEM and humanities magnet schools unfairly elevates Black and Latino students for admission in violation of the 14th Amendment. In 2023, the Supreme Court cited the same amendment in striking down the use of race in college admissions. But this case is narrower, asking the justices to decide a more technical question of what evidence challengers need to bring such a claim, so the court is not poised to issue a ruling on the constitutional issue.
The policy in question concerns a group of four middle schools with magnet programs.

The current programs are entered via lottery, a system introduced during the Covid pandemic. Entry to the lottery is based on how well students perform on tests when ranked against others in their school, which the plaintiffs say adversely affects Asian students in high-performing schools. The challengers have targeted that process, as well as one first introduced in 2017 (which has been discontinued) that sought to increase enrollment of children in low-poverty areas.

That program, sparked by a report that said Black and Latino students were underrepresented and Asian students overrepresented in the middle school magnet programs in Montgomery County schools, included outreach to students and a cognitive test.
The plaintiffs say both programs were explicitly aimed at increasing Black and Latino enrollment, thereby violating the Constitution’s 14th Amendment.
For Subscribers

Since the court’s 2023 decision, conservatives, including members of the court, have accused colleges and schools of trying to circumvent the ruling by introducing new admissions policies that have the same purpose but do not explicitly consider race as a factor.
For Subscribers
Similar cases reached the court, but the justices declined to take them up.
A federal judge in Maryland and the 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals both ruled in favor of the school district.

It’s the second time in recent years the court has heard a case challenging policies in Montgomery County Public Schools. Last year, the court ruled in favor of parents who objected on religious grounds to LGBTQ-themed books approved for use in elementary school classrooms.

title: High spirits: Supreme Court to decide fate of federal ban on home distilling
summary: The Supreme Court announced it will consider whether to strike down a longstanding federal ban on distilling spirits at home.
story: WASHINGTON — In a boost for those who want to make whiskey in their bathtubs or gin in their kitchens, the Supreme Court on Monday announced it will consider whether to strike down a long-standing federal ban on distilling spirits at home.

Although interest in the home distilling of hooch has continued despite the 150-year old ban, advocates hope the court will remove the threat of criminal sanctions, which can include a fine of up to $10,000 and a maximum sentence of five years in prison.
For decades, people have been able to make wine and beer at home for personal use without any penalties.
The distilling ban was enacted in 1868 in a bid to counter tax evasion by those making spirits. It bars the distilling of spirits in “any dwelling house” or surrounding structures.

The challengers include the Hobby Distillers Association and several of its members. One, Scott McNutt, has a still at home that he has used to distill fuel alcohol. Another, Rick Morris, owns a company that manufactures stills that can be used at home.

They sued in Texas after being told by the federal Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau, part of the Treasury Department, that they could not obtain a license to distill at home because of the federal ban.
The lawsuit contains several claims, including that Congress exceeded its taxing power by passing a ban that did not actually raise any revenue.
In a separate challenge brought in Ohio, another would-be home distiller, John Ream, raised similar claims.

The two cases resulted in conflicting rulings by federal appeals courts. In the Texas case, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals backed the challengers, while in the Ohio case, the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals reached the opposite conclusion.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
As a result, both losing parties appealed, and all parties agreed the Supreme Court should issue a definitive ruling that would apply nationwide.
If the challengers win, they would still have to register their stills and pay excise tax on the spirits they produce, even though it would be for their own consumption.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer, representing the federal government, defended the law in court papers, saying that it is within the power of Congress to restrict taxable activities by location if there is a strong chance the taxes will not be paid.

Similar to marijuana, which remains broadly illegal under federal law while various states have legalized it, several states allow home distilling, including West Virginia, which legalized it in 2024. Those laws do not take precedence over the federal ban.
Legislation has also been introduced in Congress to repeal the federal restrictions.

title: Dramatic images show violent unrest sweeping across France
summary: France unrest protest photos over the weekend Macron election buildup
story: Widespread violence erupted across France over the weekend, as rioters and looters ransacked storefronts, clashed with police and set fire to municipal buildings.
Nearly 2,400 people were arrested and almost 1,000 police officers and firefighters were injured, the French Interior Ministry said, after some of the worst unrest the country has seen in years.

title: Ukraine claims world’s first drone evacuation of wounded soldier
summary: Ukraine has shared a video showing what it says is the world’s first evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontlines by drone.
story: Ukraine has shared a video showing what it says is the world’s first evacuation of an injured soldier from the frontlines by drone.
The “historic” mission comes just as Kyiv faces a dire turn in its relationship with Washington over the withdrawal of support in its fight against Russia.

Shared by the 92nd Separate Assault Brigade on Monday, the video shows the soldier strapping himself into a large drone and being flown at what appears to be relatively low altitude over blurred-out territory. The drone carefully lowers him down and the drone operator greets him with “Welcome back to the ground!” The video also showed blurred faces of drone operators who carried out the mission.

The post said the unidentified infantryman was wounded while at his position. “Due to intense enemy drone activity and the presence of landmines, evacuation using conventional unmanned ground vehicles was impossible,” the brigade said.
Injured Ukrainian soldier rescued with a drone
“At that point, the specialists in our unit took it upon themselves to attempt something that had never been done before: evacuating a serviceman using an aerial drone,” it added.
The craft used was a heavy-lift hexacopter, it said, originally designed as a bomber by a Ukrainian manufacturer. It looks about twice the size of the soldier in the video.
The specialists working on the mission had to ensure the drone could carry a human being without flipping over or swaying excessively, according to the unit.

The rescued soldier is currently undergoing treatment and rehabilitation, the brigade added. The squad leader and programmer with the brigade, only identified by his call sign Napalm, called the soldier a “hero” for agreeing to the mission, “having seen and heard the kind of machine that had arrived to get him.”
In a separate statement, Ukraine’s Ground Forces said its drone units are already conducting operations “that were recently considered science fiction.”
The war has increasingly become a technological arms race, with both Ukraine and Russia relying on drones to reduce human casualties.

The conflict has taken a severe toll on both armies, although neither side reports up-to-date numbers of those killed, injured or missing. Ukraine in particular has faced a severe shortage of manpower as it has tried to ramp up recruitment.

Ukraine had a major leap in drone technology this year, allowing it to limit Russian logistics in occupied territories as well as strike deeper inside Russia to target Russian oil refineries, commercial warehouses and data centers.
“This mission proves once again that Ukrainian service members, working in tandem with Ukrainian manufacturers, are setting global trends in the conduct of warfare,” the brigade’s statement added.

Despite hoping that its drone innovation would give it the upper hand at the negotiating table, Kyiv has faced pressure from the U.S. to halt its strikes on Russian oil sites after President Donald Trump signed a diesel deal with the Kremlin earlier this month.
Kyiv has since also reported gaps in intelligence sharing and restrictions on Elon Musk’s Starlink service that is crucial for its drone missions, battlefield communications and air defense.

The drone evacuation comes just days after Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced the Ukrainian government had approved an “experimental project” to use drones for medical logistics. Koretskyi said flights would require coordination with the military, and drones would be given a special status and would be identifiable in the air.

“During the war, moving medical cargo by road can cost critical time, especially for transplants,” he said. “Drones will be able to carry medicines, medical products, blood samples, and donor organs between hospitals, including from remote areas.”

title: France moves to impose curfews as it reels from worst violence in years
summary: Only shattered glass and the skeletal frame of the Haussmannian roof remain of Limoges’ 19th-century town hall.
story: Only shattered glass and the skeletal frame of the Haussmannian roof remain of Limoges’ 19th-century town hall.
The town was among the places hit hardest by the rioting and looting that erupted across France over the weekend, leaving the country reeling from its worst violence in years.

The towering spire at the heart of Limoges ultimately collapsed in flames, drawing cheers from the crowd below that were captured on video. In Paris, the Louvre Museum said it was closed after protesters announced their blockade of the iconic tourist site.
Authorities conceded they had “lost control” in major cities, and said Monday they had asked some cities to impose a partial curfew in a bid to restore order.

“Despite scenes of severe violence and extensive property damage, no one was killed and that is a miracle,” Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said after an emergency meeting with top officials. About 3,000 businesses had been looted or vandalized, he added.

The unrest came on the heels of an anti-government movement that had seen days of largely peaceful protests over rising living costs and poor school conditions. On the weekend, this unrest descended into violence on the streets of cities across France: Rioters, often hooded and masked, looted stores and torched cars and government buildings as they faced off with the police.

title: Russians locked out of bank accounts and apartments as Ukraine hits data centers
summary: From accessing their money to ordering a taxi or takeout — millions of Russians were feeling the impact of Ukrainian strikes on the data centers of the country’s internet giant Yandex in their daily life.
story: From accessing their money to ordering a taxi or takeout — millions of Russians were feeling the impact of Ukrainian strikes on the data centers of the country’s internet giant Yandex in their daily life.

“I ended up in a situation where I had absolutely no money. Well, I had the money, but it was inaccessible,” said Irina, a blogger from St. Petersburg, who had not been able to access her money for four days when she spoke with NBC News last week.

Irina, who like several other interviewees did not want her last name shared while speaking with a foreign news organization on a sensitive matter, said her rent was due the day the first outages happened, when she hoped “that it would be fixed in a few hours.” Days later, she still had no access to money to pay for utilities or even food for her small child.
The strikes that took place over several days earlier this month were the first publicized attacks on Russian data centers as Ukraine seeks to bring the war home for Russians.

The disruption hit a myriad of services provided by Yandex, a tech giant akin to Google whose services are deeply integrated into daily life in Russia, and whose digital infrastructure is relied on by other third-party platforms.

Many people took to social media to complain about not being able to order a taxi or food delivery. Others reported not being able to access their files on the company’s storage service, while some even struggled to get into their homes after their digital keys went offline.

title: NFL Week 6: The return of Caleb Williams, and life gets worse for the Rams
summary: Week 6 of the NFL season featured a star player returning from one the season’s most dramatic injuries, an important game across the pond, and another devastating loss for a Super Bowl contender.
story: Week 6 of the NFL season featured a star player returning from one the season’s most dramatic injuries, an important game across the pond, and another devastating loss for a Super Bowl contender.
Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday.
Caleb Williams picked up where he left off

Chicago Bears starting quarterback Caleb Williams played Sunday for the first time since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 2, and he was spectacular in a 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and one touchdown, improving his completion percentage to 72.5% for the season.

Williams was especially efficient when not facing pressure. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Williams completed all 24 of his passes from a clean pocket, the most attempts without an incompletion under such circumstances since 2018.

After going 2-1 without their starter, the Bears improved to 4-2 with the win. The offense has been humming with Williams under center, averaging 31.0 points per game in his three starts. Chicago will now enter a spotlighted stretch of its season, as the team’s next three games will all be played in primetime.
The Rams are still searching for answers
Six weeks after entering the season as a heavy favorite to win the Super Bowl, the Los Angeles Rams (2-4) are in last place in the NFC West after Sunday’s 18-16 home loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

After a frustrating day with little offense, the Rams had finally pieced together a productive drive to tie the game at 15-all in the fourth-quarter’s final minute. The point-after was no foregone conclusion. The team cut kicker Harrison Mevis after a miss in last week’s loss to Buffalo, only to see his replacement, Blake Grupe, get hurt trying to make a tackle early Sunday. That left Rams punter Ethan Evans to step up to attempt his first point-after since college — which he made to give Los Angeles a one-point lead with 47 seconds left.

It was a different kicker who ended up the hero, though. A controversial penalty on the Rams for unnecessary roughness — a penalty that increased the Cardinals’ win probability from 26% to 74% — helped Arizona’s final drive move downfield in position for Chad Ryland to attempt a game-winning kick from 43 yards. He nailed it to keep the Rams still looking for any consistency. By the way: The Rams and Chargers have one win combined inside their home stadium, SoFi Stadium, this season. The Cardinals are 2-0 there.
The Texans’ season isn’t over just yet

The Houston Texans are winners of two straight after a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. This was the first game of the day on Sunday, and perhaps the best. Quarterbacks C.J. Stroud and Trevor Lawrence combined for 618 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Stroud was nearly perfect, posting a quarterback rating of 96.9 (out of a possible 100).
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

After the Texans opened up a 10-point lead in the final minute of the third quarter, the Jaguars stormed back. First, Lawrence led a nine-play, 61-yard touchdown drive to cut the score to 31-28 early in the fourth. Then, after a Travis Hunter interception, Lawrence led a 38-yard drive that culminated in a 60-yard field goal from Cam Little.

But Houston got the last laugh. After Little’s kick, the Texans quickly marched into Jacksonville territory on their ensuing possession. Ka’imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired, securing Houston’s second win of the season.

The Texans are now 2-4, and while their climb into playoff position will be an arduous one, Houston did make the postseason after an 0-3 start a year ago. If Stroud maintains his current level of play — he’s thrown nine touchdowns and only one interception so far this season — the Texans won’t be a pushover.
The Titans rose from the ranks of the winless

Tennessee’s season-long nightmare is finally over. The Titans finally won a game, knocking off their divisional rival the Indianapolis Colts 26-20. Tennessee stormed back in the second half, scoring all of its points in the final 30 minutes, including 20 in the final quarter.

The Colts aided the cause with a litany of mistakes. Quarterback Daniel Jones threw two interceptions, running back Jonathan Taylor had a fumble, the special teams had a punt blocked for a touchdown, and the offense also had a turnover on downs for good measure.
The Titans are now 1-5. Indianapolis, meanwhile, entered this season with high expectations from ownership, but fell to 2-4 after the loss.

title: How to watch the 2026 NBA season even if you don’t have cable
summary: Here’s everything you need to know about the 2026 NBA season, including when it starts and where to watch or stream the games.
story: Basketball fans, the NBA is almost back. This week marks the end of pre-season and the official start of the 2026-2027 basketball season, where all 30 teams will compete for a chance to win the coveted NBA Championship.

Ahead of Opening Night, I’ve gathered everything you need to know about the upcoming start to the NBA season, including where to watch and everything you need to ring in the basketball season the right way.
When is the 2026 NBA season?

The 2026-27 NBA regular season goes from October 20, 2027 until April 11, 2027. The league starts up this week with a triple-header on Tuesday, featuring the Boston Celtics versus the Detroit Pistons at 3 p.m. ET, the Philadelphia 76ers versus the New York Knicks at 7 p.m. ET and the Oklahoma Thunder versus the San Antonio Spurs closing out the day at 9:30 p.m ET.
You can check the NBA website for the full match schedule along with league standings, team stats and more.

ESPN

ESPN has one of the largest sports streaming platforms, and you can access NBA game streams nationally on ESPN and ABC via the ESPN app. You can also access ESPN+, ABC on ESPN, SEC+ ACCNX and more. You can purchase ESPN Unlimited for $31.99 per month, or pay $319.99 for the year on an annual plan.
Amazon Prime

Prime Video will show Friday night NBA games during the regular season, along with the Emirates NBA Cup Group Play stages in October and November. Amazon Prime offers a 30-day free trial that lets you take it for a test run, which includes access to games and all of Prime Video’s shows, movies and live sports library. You’ll also get all the perks of an Amazon Prime membership — following the trial, membership is $14.99 per month or $139 annually.

You can use Peacock to stream around 100 regular-season games, including Opening Night, all Monday night games, Holiday Hoops and matchups on Martin Luther King Jr. Day and Presidents’ Day. Peacock subscriptions that include live sports start at $12.99 per month or $129.99 per year for the Premium, ad-supported tier and go to $19.99 per month or $199.99 per year for the Premium Plus ad-free tier.

What are the wellness benefits of weighted stuffed animals?

Similar to weighted blankets, research shows that the benefits of weighted stuffed animals center around something called deep pressure therapy, which involves asserting gentle pressure on the body to induce feeling safe, cozy and calm. “They both provide pressure the same way a hug, massage or baby swaddle would,” says Schneeberg. And while people anecdotally say weighted blankets and weighted stuffed animals make them feel less anxious or stressed, as well as help them sleep, there’s no hard research supporting one or the other, says Dr. Alex Dimitriu, a board-certified psychiatrist and sleep medicine specialist and founder of Menlo Park Psychiatry & Sleep Medicine. Frequently asked questions

Weighted stuffed animals are a playful riff on weighted blankets, says Schneeberg. They typically clock in between one pound and five pounds, and are often filled with materials like dried flaxseed, beads or layers of fabric to get their heft.

Though anyone can use a weighted stuffed animal, they tend to be geared towards children because they are smaller than weighted blankets and can be hugged or placed on your lap for a calming effect. Weighted stuffed animals typically weigh less than weighted blankets — which start around five pounds and can go up to 40 pounds or more — and are smaller.

Because they are heavier, weighted blankets are often too large and heavy for kids to maneuver by themselves, while weighted stuffed animals are smaller, lighter and similar to other toys they may already have at home, says Dimitriu. For this reason, they can also be good for the elderly or adults who may not have the strength to maneuver a heavier blanket.

title: Why are your favorite beauty brands ditching talc?
summary: Regulations on talc in cosmetics have been causing reformulations across beauty products. I spoke to cosmetic chemists and dermatologists about potential safety issues and whether you should shop talc-free.
story: Talc has been in your favorite eyeshadows, setting powders and blushes for decades, but you may have recently spotted the phrase “talc-free” when scanning product labels. Why are popular brands like Charlotte Tilbury, Nars and Laura Mercier moving away from the ingredient that has long served a functional purpose in cosmetics, and does choosing a talc-free product actually matter?

I spoke to cosmetic chemists and board-certified dermatologists about the concerns surrounding talc, plus everything you should know when shopping for makeup. I also rounded up some talc-free products that brands have recently reformulated or always had in their lineup.

What is talc’s purpose in cosmetics?

Talc typically functions as a texture ingredient in powder-based color cosmetics like eyeshadows, powders and blushes. It helps powders feel smooth, blend evenly and resist caking, and it may help absorb oil and reduce shine, says Dr. Alexandra Bowles, a board-certified dermatologist at MONA Dermatology.

Talc is also generally well tolerated by most skin types and isn’t a common cause of allergic reactions, experts say. “When someone does react to a powder, fragrance, preservatives or other ingredients in the formula are often more likely to be responsible,” says Bowles.

The appeal of talc is that it’s incredibly versatile and multifunctional, says Esther Olu, a cosmetic chemist and licensed esthetician. “It’s also relatively inexpensive, widely available and compatible with a variety of other cosmetic ingredients,” she says. That includes pigments (it can even help distribute them and increase color payoff, says Olu), dry powders and binders like silica. While talc as an ingredient tends to be gentle on the skin, the concern usually lies in sourcing and testing.
What does the current scientific evidence say about the safety of talc in cosmetics?

The science is generally mixed. In 2019, FDA testing found trace amounts of asbestos in nine talc-containing cosmetic products, including Johnson & Johnson’s talc-based baby powder and some cosmetic products sold at Claire’s, which were voluntarily recalled. A wave of lawsuits over asbestos-contaminated talc followed. In 2024, the WHO’s cancer agency classified talc as “probably carcinogenic,” citing limited but consistent evidence for ovarian cancer. But at the same time, recent FDA testing of cosmetic samples has repeatedly come back negative for asbestos.

When people talk about talc and safety, dose and application is an important piece of context that’s usually missing from the conversation. “The ovarian-cancer data comes largely from women using loose powder in the genital area daily for decades, which is a world apart from pressed powder on your eyelids. Headlines rarely make that distinction,” says Dr. Gina Maccarone, a triple board-certified cosmetic surgeon and founder of The Surgeonista.

The “probable carcinogen” classification can also be easy to misread. “It describes whether something may be capable of causing cancer under certain conditions, not how likely it is at everyday levels of exposure,” says Bowles. Many people seem to assume talc and asbestos are interchangeable, but they’re distinct minerals that can occur together in nature. “Talc on its own isn’t considered toxic, but contamination can happen when it’s mined near asbestos deposits,” says Bowles. “As a result, where the talc comes from and how it’s tested may matter more than whether it appears on the label.”

It can help to think about the ingredient and the supply chain separately. Contamination has been documented, but it’s relatively uncommon, experts say. “I usually suggest looking for brands that share where their talc comes from and whether it undergoes independent asbestos testing,” says Bowles. In late 2024, the FDA proposed a new rule requiring manufacturers to test talc-containing cosmetics for asbestos contamination. A year later, the FDA withdrew that proposal due to legal and testing complexities.
So why are beauty brands going talc-free?

Regulation and consumer concern both appear to be driving the change. The European Union is moving toward banning talc in cosmetics in 2027, and many brands may be reformulating globally rather than making separate versions.

“The underlying worry tends to be about contamination rather than talc itself, since talc is mined and can occur near asbestos deposits. I think of the shift as a response to trust and regulation rather than a sign that talc is harming the skin,” says Bowles. However, “brands aren’t waiting for the science to fully settle,” says Maccarone. “Reformulating to talc-free is cheaper than the reputational and legal risk, so brands are getting ahead of it.”

Reformulation based on changing regulations isn’t new in the beauty world. In fact, changing formulas have been one of the biggest trends in beauty this year (my favorite Skinceuticals C E Ferulic Serum being one of them). For example, Neutrogena rolled out a new, reformulated Hydro Boost line in Europe and North America without cyclic silicones (like cyclopentasiloxane and cyclomethicone) ahead of EU bans due to environmental concerns. Similarly, bestsellers like the Armani Beauty Luminous Silk Foundation, Charlotte Tilbury Magic Cream and Bobbi Brown Cosmetics Vitamin Enriched Face Base all reformulated this year to comply with silicone regulations.

“When a major market changes its regulations, global brands must decide whether to reformulate products across their entire portfolio or maintain different formulations for different markets,” says cosmetic chemist Ava Perkins.

Plus, the packaging is stunning, so I store it proudly on top of my vanity.
Should you throw out your talc-containing cosmetics?

It’s a personal choice, but all of my experts agree: Don’t panic-buy talc-free products. “It’s a reasonable, low-cost choice if it gives you peace of mind, and good talc-free alternatives exist. But tossing every product in a frenzy isn’t warranted by the evidence,” says Maccarone. Pressed powders, blushes and eyeshadows from reputable brands tend to carry a low risk, says Bowles. You can also check whether a brand shares its asbestos-testing practices to help guide your decision.
If you do want to replace your talc-containing products, start with loose powders and any body powders, then replace other products gradually as they run out or expire, says Bowles.

Keep in mind that the importance of the “talc-free” label in the beauty industry is heavily influenced by marketing and consumer perception, experts say. The label itself tends to have an underlying meaning. “It’s the implication that a product is inherently safer simply because it doesn’t contain talc,” says Olu. “Brands understand that consumers are increasingly paying attention to ingredient lists, and removing controversial ingredients can become a way to differentiate products in a competitive market.” However, products containing talc are not automatically unsafe, says Olu.
Frequently asked questions

Talc alternatives usually include synthetic fluorphlogopite, mica, kaolin, boron nitride, silica and starches like cornstarch and rice flour. Depending on the formulation, chemists may also use ingredients like magnesium stearate, zinc stearate or other functional powders to get more specific performance characteristics, says Olu. “In many cases, replacing talc requires a combination of ingredients rather than relying on a single substitute,” she says.

However, even talc replacements can have their own concerns. “Mica can raise sourcing concerns, and cornstarch may not be ideal for body use in warm, humid skin folds, since it can potentially support yeast growth,” says Bowles. “So, a ‘talc-free’ label doesn’t necessarily mean a product is better suited to every skin type.”.

While alternatives can reproduce some of the benefits of talc (like oil absorption, blendability and slip), finding a single ingredient that replicates all of them is much more challenging, especially while staying within budget, says Perkins. “It’s really hard to get a one-to-one replacement for talc,” she says. “For example, mica may have okay oil absorption, but it won’t produce the same finish as talc. Starches may be useful to bulk a powder formula, but they can be cakey.”

It might. For example, loose powders are inhalable, so any airborne risk is higher, while pressed powders bind the particles, so far less becomes airborne, says Maccarone. “If you’re worried about inhalation, pressed is the safer format,” she says.

People with asthma or other respiratory conditions may benefit from limiting loose powders in general, says Bowles. Others who might also benefit from talc-free cosmetics include people who frequently use loose powder (especially if you apply it with a large brush that disperses more particles), makeup artists who may be around airborne powder for long stretches and anyone who uses powder on the body, particularly in the genital area.
Check the full ingredients list on the product’s packaging for the word “talc” or alternative names like magnesium silicate, talcum or talcum powder.

A common concern for brands is usually pricing, both when reformulating an existing product and finding alternatives. “Talc is relatively inexpensive and multifunctional, which makes it economically attractive for manufacturers,” says Olu. Some alternatives, like specialty grades of boron nitride, surface-treated powders and engineered silica particles, can be much more expensive. “However, not every talc-free alternative is expensive. Ingredients such as certain starches or mineral fillers can be relatively economical. The final cost depends on the ingredients, their concentrations, the formulation’s complexity and the manufacturing process,” says Olu.
Meet our skin care experts

At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest.
