I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected who has written about beauty and skin care for more than six years. I’ve also spent years testing new beauty products on the market. For this article, I spoke to board-certified dermatologists and cosmetic chemists about the potential risks of using talc-containing cosmetics, what the science says and whether you should look for talc-free alternatives. I also gathered some talc-free beauty products I’ve tested and loved, as well as favorites from NBC Selected staffers.
Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

title: McDonald’s Boo Buckets Are in Their Villain Era
summary: This Halloween, McDonald’s is partnering with Disney to produce Disney Villains Boo Buckets featuring some of the most well-known cartoon villains of all time.
story: McDonald’s is bringing back its iconic Boo Buckets for Halloween — but with a wicked twist this time around.
The fast-food chain has partnered with Disney to make Disney Villains Boo Buckets, featuring some of the most well-known cartoon villains of all time.
Whether you’re picking up a few for your kids or you simply want to relive your own childhood, here’s everything you need to know about the new release.
Disney Villains Boo Buckets Happy Meals Are Available Starting Oct. 20

McDonald’s customers can start ordering the Disney Villains Boo Buckets Happy Meal at their local restaurant starting Tuesday, Oct. 20. If you have your heart set on getting one, act fast, because they’ll only be available for a limited time, while supplies last.
There Are Five Designs in Total
Disney and McDonald’s designed five collectible Boo Buckets for the 2026 Halloween season. Each of the colorful buckets features one of the following iconic Disney villains:
JafarCruella Scar Ursula Maleficent
Jafar
Cruella
Scar
Ursula
Maleficent
According to McDonald’s Menu Spotter, the buckets come with a “villain-inspired lids” plus stickers with “iconic characters and details true fans will recognize.”
“Whether you’re into fabulous flair, mystical magic, fierce ambition, royal schemes, or sea-witch swagger, there’s a Boo Bucket for every kind of Villains fan,” reads the announcement.
Boo Buckets Have Been Making a Comeback in Recent Years

If you grew up in the ’90s, McDonald’s Boo Buckets likely hold a special place in your heart. They first appeared in 1986 but were all the rage in the ’90s as kids flocked to their local Mickey D’s to order a Happy Meal and see which Boo Bucket they’d get.
The design of Boo Buckets has changed a lot over time. They started out as a trio of orange-only designs then later featured ghost designs.
In recent years, the design has changed several times. They made a comeback in 2022 with slightly different witch, pumpkin and ghost designs than the ones fans were used to in the ’90s.
The following year, McDonald’s debuted four new Boo Buckets in the following designs: Monster (green), Skeleton (orange), Mummy (white) and Vampire (purple).
Many McDonald’s fans weren’t psyched about the 2024 Boo Buckets, which included white, orange, green and blue monster designs.
The fast-food chain made up for it in 2025 by releasing 15 Boo Buckets, with designs ranging from returning options like ghosts, pumpkins and goblins, to cats and zombies.

title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Reviews: What Critics Are Saying About the Elizabeth Holmes Doc
summary: What are critics saying about the Elizabeth Holmes docuseries? Here are reviews.
story: Crowds were eager to see everything about the story of Elizabeth Holmes on the opening weekend of an anticipated documentary about the Theranos founder.

The film “You Can See Everything,” co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, opened to $15 million at the domestic box office on its opening weekend. The nearly three-hour documentary appeared on less than 900 screens across the country but sold out more than 2,000 showings.

It’s the biggest opening weekend for a non-music documentary since Michael Moore’s 2004 documentary “Fahrenheit 9/11” about the invasion of Iraq. It also had the biggest debut for any movie playing on less than 1,000 screens since “Borat” in 2006, according to the BBC.

The film traces the weeks leading up to Holmes serving her prison sentence after being convicted of four federal charges of wire fraud in January 2022 for misrepresenting to investors what the Theranos technology could do and how widely it had been adopted. Fielder is invited into Holmes’ home, where she lives with partner Billy Evans and their two young children, ahead of her incarceration.

Holmes, 42, was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison in November 2022 and has been serving her sentence at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas. Her scheduled release date is Feb. 22, 2030, after some reductions in her sentence.
“You Can See Everything” has a 98% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, so audiences soaked it up on the opening weekend.
What are the critics saying about it? Here’s what to know.
The Hollywood Reporter
Critic Angie Han writes that the film begins as a “fascinatingly intimate portrait of a deluded or disingenuous scammer” but then morphs into something deeper.
Much of the film involves the interactions between Fielder and Holmes.

Han writes that Fielder and Oppenheim are “earnestly trying to understand Holmes’ mind and motives, even if the filmmakers don’t appear to believe for a second that she’s as innocent as she says; that Holmes really is trying her best to communicate her line of thinking, even if it requires Olympic-level mental gymnastics to justify it.”

Han zeroed in on the second half of the movie as when the film “really kicks into gear” by picking the story back up two years after Holmes went to prison. Since Holmes is incarcerated and unable to speak for herself, Evans often does so on her behalf.
Han writes that the film “makes no bones about the fact that it absolutely loathes this guy,” in reference to Evans.
There also are several twists in the second half of the film, including a well-known actor playing Holmes in reenacting the scene when Fielder first met Holmes at her San Diego home.

The film “reaches for accuracy in its portrayal of a much talked-about figure,” Han writes. “It ends up asking, with plenty of humor but no small amount of wisdom, what ‘accuracy’ would even look like in the first place.”
Variety
Critic Owen Gleiberman called the movie “just about the furthest thing from a ‘pure’ documentary you’ve ever seen.”
He writes that the film “gets its hooks into you” and is more about Fielder wanting to know what makes Holmes tick rather than litigating her guilt or innocence in the Theranos saga.
Gleiberman writes that the film depicts Holmes in “a highly rarefied level of delusional thinking” about Theranos and shows the viewer “the epic nature of her willingness to lie to herself.”

He also praises the second half of the film, which comes with spoiler warnings. The acting of the person who steps in as a substitute for Holmes to re-create moments with Fielder “is eerie in its own power.”
The film does not amount to an apology for Holmes and instead serves as “a true parable for our time.”
“It overlaps reality, performance, greed, deception, and mental illness, bringing you into the head-spinning vortex where they all meet,” Gleiberman writes.
Vulture
It’s clear where critic Alison Wilmore comes down on the film, considering her review is titled, “Nathan Fielder Has Made the Movie of the Year.”
She writes that there were scenes with Holmes where Wilmore was “tempted to think she’s one of the greatest doc subjects of all time.”

Wilmore writes that “what really makes the movie so astounding, a metanarrative mille-feuille about all the ways we try to gauge the truth, is how Holmes’s freak squares with Fielder’s, and how ‘Primetime’ prodigy Lance Oppenheim, with whom Fielder shares a co-director credit, shapes the project into something shockingly cinematic.”
She calls the first half of the movie in which the filmmakers are embedded at Holmes’ house a “surreal, agonizingly intimate window.”

Wilmore sees the film as being “about performance, raising questions about whether the Holmes we see is just the latest persona of a woman who famously made herself into a doodle of a tech iconoclast to win over funders, then even more pointedly asking what it means for her public perception to be dictated by the media about her.”
Several critics mention how Holmes seems to think she’s coming off like she’s convincing people she is innocent, but it has a completely different effect.
“In ‘You Can See Everything,’ the closer we get to her, the less knowable she is — a set of pointillist dots in the shape of a person,” Wilmore writes.
USA Today
Critic Brian Truitt calls the film “mesmerizing, troubling and uncomfortable all at once.”
“There’s just an unrealness to Holmes that’s hard to shake,” he writes.

He also enjoys the twist involving the well-known actor playing Holmes, writing that “this bonkers swerve is the best thing about the movie, but it also calls into question the truth about what we’re seeing.”
Truitt called it “a well-made flick” but pumped the brakes a little on some of the lavish praise for it.
“Is it unlike most everything else out there right now? You bet. Is it unforgettable? Eh, that’s probably going a bit far,” he writes.

“It’s funny and thought-provoking in the way it explores the stories we tell ourselves vs. the way everyone else sees us. While challenging an audience is good, though, the film leans a little off-putting in the way it doesn’t play straight.”
Roger Ebert

Review Tomris Laffly of RogerEbert.com gives it four stars and calls the film “a triumphant, riveting, and continually shape-shifting piece of creative non-fiction with curiosity and a playful sense of uncomfortable humor that will be no surprise to anyone familiar with Fielder’s work.”
Laffly gives the film praise for blurring the lines between what is real and what is performance once a camera is involved.
“Through Fielder’s interactions with Holmes, we learn that she genuinely thinks she’s never told a lie before, not even a white lie,” Laffly writes.

The reviewer also notes that movie contains “a tiny suggestion that there is a smidgen of a romantic tension between Fielder and Holmes, and Fielder perhaps developed a bit of a crush on his subject.”

Like the other critics, Laffly enjoyed the twist in the second half of the film, writing that she was “shocked, entertained, alarmed, sometimes in stitches, other times trying to make sense of the vastness of a non-fiction film that might be somewhat (and rightfully) scripted in certain moments.”

She had high praise overall, writing that the film “brilliantly sits at the intersection of documentary, narrative, comedy, reality TV, and performance, where politics, mental health, femininity, and truth in the eye of the beholder intertwine.”
Los Angeles Times
Critic Amy Nicholson labels the documentary “mindbending” and writes that it “won’t bore you for a minute” of its nearly three-hour runtime.
She calls Fielder’s scenes with Holmes “pure cringe comedy” and says Fielder is “comfortable as the film’s villain.”
“You Can See Everything’ is an absorbing study of public presentation and private doubts, a documentary that asks more questions than it answers,” Nicholson writes.
Nicholson left the theater “distrusting” Holmes and Fielder.
“I’m now as paranoid as he is — and what a pleasure,” she writes.

title: Where Is Sunny Balwani Now? Elizabeth Holmes’ Ex-Partner
summary: What to know about Elizabeth Holmes’ ex and Theranos’ former president and chief operating officer Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani.
story: Elizabeth Holmes is back in the spotlight due to her involvement in the documentary “You Can See Everything.”
Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the nearly three-hour film shows the Theranos CEO and founder weeks before she reported to a federal prison in Texas in 2023.

While “You Can See Everything” centers around Holmes, her partner William “Billy” Evans and their two children at their home in San Diego, California, it also touches on her now-defunct company once poised to revolutionize the blood testing industry.
It also briefly looks at her romantic relationship with the company’s former president and chief operating officer Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani.

At the age of 19, Holmes dropped out of Stanford to found the biotech startup, which aimed to perform hundreds of tests using a single drop of blood. However, Theranos’ technology proved unable to follow through with its founder’s promises, despite raising over $900 million from investors.
Holmes was sentenced to 11 years in prison after being convicted of four counts of investor fraud and conspiracy. Balwani was found guilty of 12 counts of fraud and sentenced to 12 years.
The saga of Theranos played out in courts, exposés, podcasts, and shows like Hulu’s “The Dropout” that covered Holmes and Balwani’s history together.
Below, find out more about Sunny Balwani, including where he is now.
Sunny Balwani and Elizabeth Holmes’ Relationship Began in Beijing
Balwani and Holmes’ first meeting took place during Stanford’s Mandarin language immersion program Beijing in 2002, according to “Bad Blood” by John Carreyrou.

They were in different phases of life. Holmes, 18, was heading into her freshman year at Stanford. Balwani was 37. A software executive, Balwani made a fortune before the dotcom bubble burst in 2000, earning about $40 million in the acquisition of his company per the New York Times.
He Started Working for Theranos in 2009
In 2004, Holmes left Stanford University to start Theranos. In 2017, Balwani revealed he gave Holmes a personal loan to use for Theranos in 2009.

“The company was low on cash, and I knew of the mission and that what the company was trying to do was paramount, and I offered to help the company, and I ended up giving a $13 million personal loan,” he explained in a 2017 deposition, obtained on ABC’s “The Dropout” podcast. “It was interest-free. It was a good-faith loan.”

Six months after giving the personal loan, Balwani became the president and COO of Theranos. As prospectors pointed out during his trial per NBC, Balwani “had no medical degree, no experience in blood testing, (and) no experience building medical devices or running a lab.”
Balwani worked at Theranos until 2016, per the Justice Department.
Holmes and Balwani Had a Romantic Relationship
Unbeknownst to Theranos investors or employees, Holmes and Balwani were carrying out a romantic relationship, and had lived together since 2005, per “Bad Blood.”
In testimony given during her trial, Holmes claimed that Balwani had emotionally and sexually abused her. Balwani has denied all abuse accusations.
Balwani Faced the Same Charges as Holmes and Pled Not Guilty to All

Balwani’s trial began in California in March 2022 and ended on July 7 with a guilty verdict. The disgraced executive faced two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, as well as nine counts of actual wire fraud.
According to U.S. v. Elizabeth Holmes, et al., the charges stemmed from accusations that Balwani and Holmes took part in a multi-million-dollar scheme to defraud investors, doctors and patients.

Similar to Holmes’ separate trial (which ended in January 2022), a jury was asked to determine whether Balwani intended to deceive Theranos’ investors about patients about the capabilities of the company’s blood-testing machines, or if he was unaware of their foibles the entire time.

During the trial’s opening statements on March 22, a federal prosecutor cast Balwani as Holmes’ right-hand man, helping sell investors, patients, and health providers on Theranos’ machines’ testing capabilities.

Conversely, Balwani’s lawyer Stephen Cazares, according to the New York Times, chose to deflect blame onto Holmes in his opening statement. “Sunny Balwani did not start Theranos. He did not control Theranos. Elizabeth Holmes, not Sunny, founded Theranos and built Theranos,” Cazares said.
Balwani Was Found Guilty of 12 Counts of Fraud

In early July, the former top executive of Theranos was convicted of fraud for misleading investors about the financial health of the health care startup, according to NBC News. Balwani was convicted on all 12 counts of wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
Balwani and Holmes’ Texts Gave Insight Into Their Relationship
During both Holmes and Balwani’s trials, text exchanges were submitted as evidence. According to NBC, the texts amounted to 12,000 total.

Some texts showed how they perceived their relationship. In one 2014 exchange shared during Holmes’ trial per the Washington Post, Balwani wrote, “I love you. I admire your wisdom and your strength; and your decency and kindness.” Holmes replied, “You know what these things coming from you mean to me. What you say to me equals my confidence.”

Other texts showed their approach to the business. In April 2022, NBC provided an exchange included in Balwani’s trial, in which Balwani texted Holmes, “...this business…that’s why the universe brought us together.” Holmes replied, “I know.”
In another text, sent in July 2015, Balwani wrote, “I am responsible for everything at Theranos,” per NBC.
Balwani Sold the Home He Shared With Holmes
Court testimony revealed that in 2013, Balwani and Holmes created an LLC to purchase a $9 million, five-bedroom, seven-bathroom home based in Atherton, California.
According to Market Watch, Balwani sold the house for $15.8 million in Jan. 2022.
Balwani Reports to Prison
Balwani reported to prison in April 2023, according to CNN.
He is currently at FCI Lompoc II, a low-security federal prison in Lompoc, California.
He is scheduled to be released on April 21, 2033, according to the prison record.

title: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026: Full List of Models and Performers
summary: The 2026 Victoria’s Secret fashion show was full of heavenly moments and a few fun surprises.
story: The 2026 Victoria’s Secret fashion show was full of heavenly moments and a few fun surprises.
On Oct. 18, the lingerie and clothing brand showed off its latest collection in the fashion show, which was livestreamed from Los Angeles on the Victoria’s Secret YouTube and social media channels.

For years, the show was an annual event, but it took a multiyear hiatus after being canceled in 2019 due to declining ratings and controversy. The 2026 fashion show marks the third event since its grand return in 2024.
Missed the live show? Here are some of the biggest stars who walked the runway:
Barbara Palvin

After welcoming her first child in September, Barbara Palvin wasted no time returning to work. The new mom was glowing as she walked down the aisle in pretty pink lingerie as her husband, Dylan Sprouse, cheered from the audience.
This is hardly the first time Palvin has proved that she’s made of tough stuff. In 2025, she appeared in the fashion show four weeks after breaking her foot.
Natalia Bryant
Natalia Bryant, the daughter of late NBA star Kobe Bryant, brought some sparkle to the runway as she sported several items from Victoria’s Secret’s PINK collection.

The 23-year-old, who had made her runway debut in 2023, rocked a black and pink bra, pink velvet shrug sweater, jeans with colorful rhinestones, heels, sparkly silver purse and oversized heart earrings.
Kylie Jenner

Near the end of the show, one model began to walk down the runway as the lights dimmed to shield her identity. When the lights returned, it became clear that it was none other than Kylie Jenner. The reality star and entrepreneur was entrusted to debut Victoria’s Secret’s 2026 Fantasy Bra, which costs $50 million, per Vogue.

As she walked down the runway, Jenner waved to the crowd as her oversized white angel wings were on full display. In the audience, her proud mom Kris Jenner and beau Timothée Chalamet were beaming as they cheered.
According to Us Weekly, Jenner is the first non-Victoria’s Secret Angel to wear the Fantasy Bra in a runway show. The brand’s chief creative officer, Adam Selman, told Vogue why she was selected.

“Kylie really extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV, beyond one singular thing,” he said. “That’s the exact same thing that we do. Like, the show is so big, it’s true entertainment, and I think that she is a great catalyst for that.”
Trinity Rodman
Soccer star Trinity Rodman made her Victoria’s Secret show debut wearing a cropped black tank and boyshorts from the PINK collection.

Rodman, daughter of basketball player Dennis Rodman, plays for the Washington Spirit in the National Women’s Soccer League. Just one day before the fashion show, Rodman and the Spirit defeated Gotham FC to clinch a playoff spot.

While Rodman’s boyfriend, tennis star Ben Shelton, was not able to attend the show in person due to training, she sent him a sweet message beforehand, telling “Entertainment Tonight,” “love you and wish you were here.”
Tate McRae
Singer Tate McRae looked red-hot as she performed her hit “Housewife” in head-to-toe red, including sparkly lingerie, stilettos and a red microphone.
During her next song, “Sports Car,” McRae donned an oversized pair of translucent red angel wings. She ended her performance by walking the runway and blowing a kiss to the camera.
Alex Consani

Alex Consani made her third Victoria’s Secret fashion show appearance at the 2026 event. In 2024, the model made history alongside Valentina Sampaio as they became the first transgender women to walk in the show, per Harper’s Bazaar.
This year, Consani modeled a pale pink bra and matching underwear.
KATSEYE

Four members of the group KATSEYE performed their hits “Pinky Up” and “Animal” as models donned designs from Victoria’s Secret’s PINK collection. The group wore black and pink ensembles with plenty of sparkle.
Megan Moroney

Megan Moroney was the first musical performance of the night.  She appeared on stage in pale pink sparkly lingerie with matching angel wings and a pink microphone as she sang her hit “6 Months Later.” The singer also treated the audience to a performance of her song “Sorry… I Meant Tonight.”
Megan Thee Stallion

Megan Thee Stallion exuded confidence during her performance. The rapper showed off plenty of skin in a sparkly bra, black thong, thigh-high stockings and heels. She paired the look with oversized angel wings. The musician performed two of her biggest hits: “Her” and “Body.”

title: Cindy Crawford Breaks Silence on Death of Son Presley Gerber: ‘Til We Meet Again Our Sweet Boy’
summary: Cindy Crawford is paying tribute to her son Presley Gerber who died in September.
story: Cindy Crawford is paying tribute to her son Presley Gerber who died in September.

For the first time since Gerber’s death, Crawford addressed the tragedy in a moving Instagram post shared Oct. 18. The mom of two wrote that the family is “beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother.”

“We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years. He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever,” she wrote in the Instagram post. “We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.”
Presley Gerber, a model himself, is one of two children that Crawford shares with her husband, businessman Rande Gerber. The couple has a younger daughter, model and actor Kaia Gerber, who is 25.

Presley Gerber died Sept. 20 at a rehabilitation facility, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The records show that the cause of death is pending additional investigation. No further details were provided.
In her post, Crawford thanked those who showed the family support amid the difficult time.
“We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain,” she wrote.
The former supermodel and actor concluded the post with a sweet message to her late son.
“Til we meet again our sweet boy,” Crawford wrote. “We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia 🪽”
Kaia Gerber also posted a sweet tribute to her brother on Instagram the same day. In her post, Kaia Gerber wrote to “prez” about “how much I loved being your sister.”

“it has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. i came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you,” Kaia Gerber wrote in long, open letter to her brother. “i had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole.”
In the Instagram post, she also shared a sweet throwback video of the siblings as kids, hugging and dancing together, along with a few old pictures.

“i am learning how to love you when i cannot see you. how to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you,” Kaia Gerber wrote in the heartbreaking post. “how to be your sister in a world that I can’t reach for you in. i dont know how to do that yet.”
Kaia Gerber also seemingly referenced physicist Richard Feynman’s famous letter to his late wife.
“my darling brother, i do adore you,” Kaia Gerber wrote. “i love my brother. my brother is dead. and this party sucks so bad without you, prez.”
Hours before authorities found him unresponsive, Presley Gerber had checked into rehab facility Resolutions Living of Santa Monica, a law enforcement source told NBC News.
His death is being investigated as a suspected overdose, police have said.

Gerber has been open about his struggles with depression and addiction in the past. In June, just months before his death, Gerber took part in a panel discussion about mental health, according to People magazine. It would be his final public appearance.
“The most free I felt was when I was finally honest with myself,” he told the audience.

title: Celebs Looked Like They Were Plucked From A Fairytale at Academy Museum Gala Red Carpet
summary: Celebrities on Oct. 17 attended the Academy Museum Gala, a benefit that raised funds for the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles.
story: They look straight out of a storybook!

Celebrities on Oct. 17 attended the Academy Museum Gala, a benefit that raised funds for the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles. While the night included several standout moments — including a performance by superstar Taylor Swift — one of the major highlights was the red carpet, where actors, filmmakers and more strutted their best stuff.

The benefit, which is in its sixth year, is part of the museum’s efforts to “celebrate and preserve cinema,” according to a press release about the event. The gala, co-chaired by Tom Ford, Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg, and Kate Capshaw, boasted attendees including the likes of Kim Kardashian, Demi Moore, Janelle Monae and many others.
From stunning, pearly gowns to striking velvet tuxedos, the star-studded event had no shortage of dreamy looks.
Check out some of the night’s most dazzling ensembles.
Taylor Swift

The “Patient Zero” songstress not only performed her “Toy Story 5” song, “I Knew It, I Know You,” at the event, but she also stunned — in a gray-blue floor-length custom Dior gown. She tied the look together with a pair of dangling, diamond earrings.
Demi Moore
Actor Demi Moore rocked the red carpet in a long, black and pale purple gown by fashion house Standing Ground. The look, styled by Brad Goreski, was completed with a classic updo.
Kim Kardashian

Kim Kardashian showed up to the gala in a look reminiscent of Elizabeth Taylor and the Golden Age of Hollywood. Styled by celebrity “image architect” Law Roach, Kardashian donned a 1951 vintage Balenciaga gown, along with a diamond choker and sparkling earrings.
Janelle Monae

Singer and actor Janelle Monae arrived in one of the most artistic ensembles of the night. Monae wore a sequined deep purple-and-black ombré gown, complete with a massive butterfly accent by designer Robert Wun. Her matching sheer gloves added an extra special accent to the look.
Connor Storrie
“Heated Rivalry” star Connor Storrie stunned in a long, black Saint Laurent coat and slacks. The look was tied together with a black, satin scarf and two pairs of small hoop earrings.
Camila Cabello

Singer Camila Cabello strutted her stuff in a tight, black corset that was paired with mesh skirt from Dolce & Gabbana’s 1998 Spring collection. The romantic look was tied together with a dreamy bun and long, flowing scarf that trailed behind her.
Eddie Redmayne
Actor Eddie Redmayne walked the red carpet in a Giorgio Armani royal blue, velour button-down shirt paired with pleated navy pants.
Cole Escola

“Oh, Mary!” creator Cole Escola showed up to the gala in a stunning black Chanel gown and cape that featured a giant black bow. The look was tied together with dangling, emerald earrings and a black clutch.
Alexander Skarsgard

Actor Alexander Skarsgard is known for his unique outfits and this particular look was no exception. The “Wicker” star, styled by Harry Lambert, rocked a white, ruffled button-down with a black flower accent.
Bird Runningwater
Producer Bird Runningwater rocked the red carpet in a floor-length, long-sleeved cape, white ruffled button-down and, of course, an infectious smile.
Peyton Lee
Actor Peyton Elizabeth Lee showed up to the dazzling event in a dreamy, Marco Rambaldi off-white dress.
Amandla Stenberg
Amandla Stenberg strutted the carpet, wearing a sheer, deep-V-neck gown from Zimmermann that was adorned with butterfly and flower appliques.
Tracee Ellis Ross
Actor Tracee Ellis Ross, who was styled by Law Roach, lit up the carpet with a vibrant, orange number by Balenciaga. Her hair was pulled into a tight bun in contrast to the free-flowing dress.
Inde Navarrette
Actor Inde Navarrette rocked a polka dot Schiaparelli dress that featured a bubble-shaped skirt. She tied the couture look together with some black, pointed-toe stilettos.
Ava DuVernay
Director Ava DuVernay wore an off-the-shoulder, powder blue Louis Vuitton gown, reminiscent of Cinderella.
Kendall Jenner
Model Kendall Jenner wore an all-polka dot ensemble from Valentino. The dress included a deep thigh split and polka dot bows. The look was tied together with a pair of polka dot shoes.
Pamela Anderson
Pamela Anderson wore a two-piece Carolina Herrera number that featured a white button down shirt and a long, sage green skirt.
Jaafar Jackson
“Michael” star Jaafar Jackson strutted his stuff in a classic, velvet tux look.
Anna Kendrick
Actor Anna Kendrick wore a striking black swan-esque gown from designer Georges Chakra that featured black appliques, a plunging neckline and flared hips.

title: How Skiing, Skateboarding Accidents Led To Role Model’s Booming Music Career
summary: Breaking his wrist on two separate occasions while skiing and skateboarding turned out to be happy accidents for Role Model.
story: Breaking his wrist on two separate occasions while skiing and skateboarding turned out to be happy accidents for Role Model.

The 29-year-old singer, whose real name is Tucker Pillsbury, was a freshman at Point Park University in Pittsburgh in 2014 when he busted his wrist while skiing in Maine and then again while skateboarding. It left him stuck in his dorm room, where his friends left some recording equipment.
He spoke to Willie Geist on “Sunday Sitdown” on TODAY Oct. 18 about how that moment of isolation was an inflection point in his life.

“I remember it was dark,” he told Willie. “It was those injuries and then also I really didn’t have friends in Pittsburgh at the time. I didn’t have people to talk to about the way I was feeling. I just had a microphone and a laptop in my closet, and that definitely saved me.”
Up to that point, the native of Cape Elizabeth, Maine, had been mainly passionate about filmmaking, he explained.
“I always had a camera,” he said. “I was always outside. I was filming, making skate videos and skiing videos with my friends, and then that turned into little music videos for people.”
However, once he went to college to study film, he said he realized his path in life lay elsewhere.

“Figured out I didn’t love being taught film, and so, in that moment of my freshman year when I was like, ‘I don’t like this, what do I do,’” he said. “I had come across these kids that made music in their dorm rooms. I didn’t know you could just do it yourself.  They gave me equipment, and I sat down and became obsessed with it.”
He began recording music under the name Role Model and posting it online. His songs caught the interest of the late rapper, producer and Pittsburgh luminary Mac Miller.
“It lit me up emotionally and artistically and gave me that kick that I needed,” Role Model said. “And then also it shed a light on me in the industry and labels started to kind of hear about it.’’
He has since released three studio albums, including his latest, “Chuck Timely and the Hourglass.”

The song “Sally, When the Wine Runs Out” from his previous album became a social media sensation in 2025 with viral clips of celebrities like Natalie Portman and Kate Hudson joining him onstage as “Sally.”
“If people liked that, I can do better,” he told Willie. “Now I want to really write songs that aren’t just like, ‘Cold like Minnesota, hotter than a fever.’”

Role Model added, laughing: “That bridge is like reading a children’s book. I love it though, and I’m always going to perform it. It was the best happy accident that probably happened in my career. So, I’m very thankful for it.”
The performer, who was an opening act just two years ago, is now headlining his own tour, which has two more dates in California before starting the European leg.
He is also giving acting a try. Role Model makes his debut in Lena Dunham’s new rom-com, “Good Sex,” which comes out on Netflix later this year.

title: Our 1 Question for Daisy Edgar-Jones During Commercial: Which Sarah J. Maas Character Would She Want to Play?
summary: Daisy Edgar-Jones talks her new role in “Sense & Sensibility” and her love for “ACOTAR” and the books by Sarah J. Maas.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.
Actor Daisy Edgar-Jones is a longtime Jane Austen fan, but she learned something new while bringing to life Elinor in the latest adaptation of “Sense and Sensibility.”

The book is often summarized by its title, with each of the two lead sisters representing one of the seemingly opposing virtues. Where Elinor is restrained, Marianne is passionate. Elinor is polite, Marianne is viviacious. Elinor is sense, Marianne is sensibility.
But in re-visiting the novel, and viewing it through the lens of director Georgia Oakley, Edgar-Jones argues it’s not that simple.

“Her feelings are strong, but she’s learnt how to govern them. For me that was really key: She isn’t just somebody who’s unfeeling,” Edgar-Jones says. “She’s actually extremely passionate and has this deep well of feeling.”

TODAY.com caught up with Edgar-Jones backstage at Studio 1A the week of “Sense & Sensibility’s” theatrical premiere, Oct. 16. Like her character, Edgar-Jones is poised, thoughtful in her answers and always wearing a gentle smile. But she visibly lights up and starts to speak faster when I dig into one of her favorite topics, as the world recently learned: the works of author Sarah J. Maas. Turns out, Edgar-Jones is just as passionate a romantasy (a portmanteau for the combined romance and fantasy genre) reader as she is an Austen fan.

Read on for more on Edgar-Jones’ portrayal of Elinor, her chemistry with co-star Esme Creed-Miles, who stars as Marianne, and how she’s preparing for Maas’ upcoming novel “A Court of Splintered Harmony,” out Oct. 27.

In particular with a character like Elinor, she’s somebody who feels a lot, feels very deeply. But she has learned over time how to govern that and hide her emotions from others. So it’s always a challenge playing a character like that, because you never want her restraint to feel like a lack of passion. For me, tracking that journey that she goes on, where by the end she really embraces her wildness and her inner spirit, and that bubbles over, that was really a fun challenge.

But also with Austen, her characters are so brilliantly written, and her stories are so clear in terms of their vision and their themes that really it’s about finding a filmmaker that can capture something new in her writing. (Georgia) Oakley is a really talented filmmaker, and I think that she’s brought out a kind of gritty, earthier side to Austen that we’ve not seen before, which I’m super proud of.

We all hold multitudes, and I think that’s the story, really. It’s about balance, about the fact that we need a bit of both. The two sisters go on these converging arcs. Elinor, it’s described in the book that her feelings are strong, but she’s learnt how to govern them. For me that was really key: She isn’t just somebody who’s unfeeling and sensible. She’s actually extremely passionate and has this deep well of feeling. But she’s just gotten very good at keeping that hidden.

Whereas Marianne, who does traditionally occupy sensibility, she’s actually got so much wisdom that she can give to Elinor. There’s a great line that she says, which is: “If I am to fall, I wish it to be from a great height.” Which is a great piece of wisdom for a character like Elinor, because actually she could learn to be a little more brave, in terms of taking risks and being vulnerable.
It’s a story about how these women teach each other, and gift each other, and evolve.

Yeah, I mean, I think that Elinor doesn’t have to be this cold and stern, emotionless person. That actually you can still occupy the space of sense and also — I remember there’s a line in the book that said that she had a really good sense of humor.

I never wanted, between Elinor and Marianne, her to feel like she was disapproving of Marianne’s spirit. I always wanted to make sure it was that she embraced her spirit, she just never wanted Marianne to get hurt. For me, the real learning was that the core love story of this film is the sisters. And that was a big part of what Georgia wanted to bring out of the story. That really girlhood and sisterhood is an incredibly romantic relationship you can have in your life.

I’ve known Esme a long time. We met when I was 19, and she was 17. We did our first ever indie film together, which was so wonderful because I remember loving working with Esme at that time. Meeting her again in our chemistry reads, I had such a clear idea of her 17-year-old face, you know, when I was acting across from her 25-year-old self.

So much of sisterhood is a shared history and context and a knowledge of one another. And I just — I care so deeply for Esme, and I feel very sisterly towards her. I don’t have siblings myself, so I think she’s kind of occupied that space for me now in a lovely way. Honestly, playing with her was effortless. It took no work.

Yeah, I suppose .... Hm. Feyre gives more older sister energy. Elain is definitely giving baby sister. The bonds between sisters is unique, like the love is really deep, but you can also hurt each other really deeply. When you know someone that well and family, it’s a kind of wonderful complexity of those kinds of dynamics. I just love in that story how ultimately they all band together and they support each other and fight together. That sisterly bond is unbreakable.
I love them all. I would love the challenge of Manon Blackbeak because I think that I haven’t had a chance to show my inner witch, but would love that chance to be an Ironteeth witch.
I’ve got “Kingdom of Ash” left. And then I have to read the “Crescent City” books.

Well, I don’t know. I’m like, do I need to? I mean I’m all caught up on “ACOTAR,” so I’m ready. I could dive in. But I’m like, do I get through “Crescent City,” then I’ve got all of the lore and all of the worlds, you know? We’ll see. But I feel ready.

title: Val Chmerkovskiy Hit With One-Week Suspension on ‘Dancing With The Stars’
summary: Val Chmerkovskiy will not be participating in the upcoming episode of “Dancing With The Stars.”
story: Val Chmerkovskiy will not be participating in the upcoming episode of “Dancing With The Stars.”
The show announced Oct. 17 that Chmerkovskiy, a pro on the competition who’s currently paired with actor Jenna Dewan, will be suspended for a week.

It comes after Chmerkovskiy found himself in hot water last week when he posted a status on TikTok that appeared to reference Will Smith’s notorious altercation with Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars. The pro had been reacting to the harsh critique that judge Carrie Ann Inaba gave his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson who’s paired up with actor Harry Shum Jr.
“You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” Chmerkovskiy wrote in the since-deleted status seen by NBC News.
In a statement sent to NBC News, BBC Studios, the production company behind “DWTS,” said that the “well-being of everyone who works on Dancing with the Stars is non-negotiable.”

“Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show,” the statement said. “As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show.”
Chmerkovskiy responded to the news of his suspension by posting an apology to his Instagram story. The dancer wrote that he initially intended to “defend my wife.”

“I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention,” he wrote, referencing Smith’s words to Rock amid the Oscars spat, “Keep my wife’s name out of your f------ mouth.”
Chmerkovskiy added: “Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was.”
He also had some well wishes for those on the show.
“Please send Carrie Ann, Jenna, and the whole DWTS family lots of love during Dedication Night,” he wrote. “I’ll be watching and cheering everyone on!!”
Inaba has not responded publicly to Chmerkovskiy’s apology or suspension.
Instead of performing with Chmerkovskiy, Dewan will be dancing with pro Alan Bersten in a number that’s dedicated to her mother.

Things got heated amid the Oct. 13 episode of “DWTS” when Inaba accused Johnson of incorporating a lift into her samba routine with Shum. The Latin style of dance traditionally prohibits the move — something that the judge has enforced in the past.
While Johnson, looking confused, asked, “Lift?” Inaba returned with an immediate response.

“A lift is, I just need to say it,” she said before reading off of a sheet of paper with the printed definition. “Any movement during which one of the dancers has both feet off the floor at the same time with the assistance or support of their partner. Yeah. Lift.”
Later on in the episode, Johnson appeared to take the criticism well.
“I will take it, sure,” she said.
Chmerkovskiy has previously apologized for his TikTok status. On Oct. 15, he posted on his Instagram story that he had reached out to Inaba directly to apologize.

“I recognize that I am in a fortunate position to have a platform and to be a role model to some, and I need to treat that with more care by actively pausing to think before I post to ensure what I am sharing aligns with who I am, and who I want to be for you all,” he wrote in the Instagram story.

title: Carrot Top Speaks Out For The First Time Following Suicide Attempt
summary: Comedian Carrot Top is breaking his silence, nearly a month after he was hospitalized following a suicide attempt.
story: Comedian Carrot Top is breaking his silence, nearly a month after   he was hospitalized following a suicide attempt.

The comedian, born Scott Thompson, shared an uplifting post on Instagram, thanking fans for “being there for me during this time.” He also wrote that he’ll be returning to perform Oct. 19 at the Luxor Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas, Nevada, where he has a residency.

It comes weeks after he was released from the hospital following the Sept. 18 attempt, his representatives confirmed to NBC News. Further details surrounding his condition and hospitalization have not been released to the public.

“I’m truly overwhelmed by the outpouring of love, support, prayers, and well wishes I’ve received over the past couple of weeks,” he wrote. “Every message, text, and kind thought has meant more to me than you know.”
He concluded, telling fans that the well-wishes “truly means the world to me!”
The comedian rose to fame in the 1990s after his debut on reality talent competition show “Star Search.” His appearance on the “Tonight Show” in 1995 further propelled his career.
He’s also made a number appearances in television shows, including on an episode of “Hacks” in 2024.
Most recently, he’s been performing at the Luxor Hotel as part of a residency that he has held since 2005.

title: Paul McCartney Has One Little Ask For The Upcoming ‘The Beatles’ Biopics
summary: The legendary rock star sat down with comedian Amy Poehler for the latest episode of her podcast “Good Hang” and revealed that he had a note for director Sam Mendes, whose highly anticipated series of four films about the groundbreaking band is slated to be released in 2028.
story: Paul McCartney has just ooooone little critique for the upcoming Beatles biopics.

The legendary rock star sat down with comedian Amy Poehler for the latest episode of her podcast “Good Hang.” He revealed that he had a note for director Sam Mendes, whose highly anticipated series of four films about the groundbreaking band is slated to be released in 2028.
McCartney lamented to Poehler that while all members of The Beatles are roughly the same height, his character appears to be shorter than that of John Lennon’s.
“He sent me a picture — a still from the filming they were doing, and they’re crossing the Abbey Road crossing,” McCartney said. “The Paul character is markedly smaller!”
McCartney said he just had to pick up the phone.
“I texted him, Sam,” McCartney said during the episode, released Oct. 13. “‘Don’t do this.’”

For the biopics, McCartney is being played by Paul Mescal who, according to his IMDB page, is 5’11” — not at all a short king. Harris Dickinson, who will star as John Lennon, is just pretty darn tall. His height is listed as 6’2” on his IMDB page.
Barry Keoghan will play Ringo Starr in the films while Joseph Quinn will appear as George Harrison.
In the podcast episode, McCartney admits that he’s “got a thing” about height.

“We were all the same height and Ringo was a bit smaller,” he explains. “(Director Sam Taylor-Johnson) did a film called ‘Nowhere Boy,’ and the John character, — who she later married — he’s bigger than me in the film!”
“Nowhere Boy,” released in 2009, featured Aaron Taylor-Johnson as Lennon while Thomas Brodie-Sangster played McCartney.
McCartney, who said he is still good friends with the director, recalled that she gave him an explanation.
“She said, ‘This is a movie. It’s not a documentary,’” a disgruntled McCartney says. “I thought, ‘Well, I don’t like that explanation.’ But I couldn’t do anything because by now she’d made the film.”
He added: “There was I, little Paul. And, you know, John, the great big hero. And it’s like — no! It’s not true.”

title: Miley Cyrus Breaks Down During Tribute to Dolly Parton: ‘Me and Dolly, We Are Eternal’
summary: Miley Cyrus got emotional while honoring her beloved late “Aunt Dolly” during her comeback performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.
story: Miley Cyrus got emotional while honoring her beloved late “Aunt Dolly” during her comeback performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

The singer, who made her return to the stage in her first solo show since 2022, sang a soulful rendition of Dolly Parton’s hit “Jolene.” But before Cyrus, the goddaughter of the “Queen of Country,” performed the cover, she said a few words about Parton, breaking down during the sweet tribute.
“Me and Dolly, we are eternal,” Cyrus said, speaking to the crowd as she sat at the edge of the stage. “Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart.”
Cyrus got particularly tearful when reflecting on Parton’s absence. The longtime country music icon passed away in August, following a brief battle with cancer, her estate said.
“And I’m gonna see her again,” Cyrus said. “And I can’t f------ wait. And I miss her.”

The tribute was part of Cyrus’ first performance at the iconic venue. Her second sold-out show will take place Oct. 18. The singer, who’s currently promoting her new album “Bass Persuades,” last performed a full-length concert in Mexico roughly four years ago at the Corona Capital Festival.
Her latest set of shows are particularly significant for the “Flowers” singer, who explained to the audience that she had only ever seen Parton perform live once. And it was at the Hollywood Bowl.
“Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced, performed by my Aunt Dolly,” Cyrus said, introducing “Jolene.” “This is one of those songs.”

Parton, who died at age 80, was a fixture in Cyrus’ life. The Queen of Country once toured with the singer’s father, country star Billy Ray Cyrus, and was bestowed the role of godmother upon Miley Cyrus’ birth in 1992.
During an interview with Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, released Sept. 17, Miley Cyrus opened up about the meaningful relationship she shared with Parton.

“She was always right,” Cyrus said. “It’s like how your mom’s always right, and when you’re a kid, you’re like, ‘What does she know?’ And then as you get older, you’re like, ‘Everything. How? Where did this come from? You’re just a normal person. Why do you know everything?’”
Cyrus added: “Dolly was just always right about stuff.”

title: The Shocking ‘You Can See Everything’ Twist: Wait, Who Shows Up in the Elizabeth Holmes Documentary?
summary: The documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, “You Can See Everything,” takes a surprise turn that will have viewers on the edge of their seats. Here is what happens.
story: Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes.
Thirty-four days before she was set to enter prison in 2023,Elizabeth Holmes let a film crew into her home.
“You Can See Everything,” directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is the boundary-pushing result of what the filmmakers captured — and it’s unlike anything that’s been done before.

The Theranos founder and CEO hoped to revolutionize blood testing. However, in 2022, after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab, she was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud.

Sentenced to 11 years in prison, “You Can See Everything” shows Holmes in her San Diego home with partner William “Billy” Evans and their two children, Willian and Invicta. Maintaining her innocence, Holmes let the cameras film her and her family up until she surrendered to Federal Prison Camp Bryan in Texas.
But that’s just the first half of the almost-three-hour film.
What Is the Twist In ‘You Can See Everything’?
Amid the questions that arise about Holmes, as well as her relationship with Evans, Fielder decides to reach out to none other than Amanda Seyfried for insight.
Why the actor?
Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the 2022 limited series “The Dropout,” even winning an Emmy for her performance.

During his stay at their home, Fielder has Holmes and Evans watch episodes of “The Dropout.” The show ends up making Holmes uncomfortable and through tears she tells Fielder she no longer wants to watch it.
Holmes then goes to prison, but filming continues.

Holmes and Evans had been working on a new business venture, what they called Theranos 2.0. Two years after Holmes reported to prison, Evans calls the film crew and tells them he has an update on their project.
Fielder tries to get updates about Holmes, who was unreachable with cameras, but doesn’t get much. Then tensions start brewing between Evans and the film crew.

“As we are trying to finish making (the film) ... (Evans) started trying to exert a level of control over the process that made it very hard to engage with him,” Fielder said at an Oct. 6 Los Angeles screening. “It was uncomfortable for us ... We sort of had to stop. Communication broke down basically, and we’ve been in that state for a little bit.”
Fielder noted, at the time, that Evans had not seen the film.
How Did Amanda Seyfried Get Involved in ‘You Can See Everything’?
Fielder and Oppenheim had never met Seyfried, but was one of many people they reached out to in late 2025, according to press notes.
“A lot of people say no in this process, and a lot of people who are relevant to her story want nothing to do with her anymore,” Fielder said.
Thanks to a mutual friend, Fielder was able to connect with Seyfried, who agreed to watch their footage and talk about her experience on camera.

While preparing for her role in “The Dropout,” Seyfried never met or communicated with Holmes. However, the actor became “an invaluable key” in how the filmmakers continued their investigation and the “unprecedented” ending.
About halfway through the film, after Holmes is in prison, Seyfried and Fielder watch the footage of Holmes watching “The Dropout.”
This was the first in-person meeting between the two and it was captured “as it unfolded, unscripted and in real time.”
What came next is unorthodox, unconventional and intriguing.
Seyfried accompanies Fielder to Holmes’ San Diego home where he recounts the first time he met the biotech company founder. They then re-create that very scene.
As the documentary continues, Seyfried continues to help Fielder in his re-creations, including a meeting with the filmmakers, A24 executives and Holmes and Evans.
As Seyfried’s involvement deepens, she begins to bring her own perspective to Holmes’ life, also questioning the CEO and her partner’s intentions.

In a wild turn of events, Fielder brings Seyfried to Evans’ home, where she gets a chance to briefly speak with Holmes who calls from prison. After some shocking revelations, including Evans controlling Holmes’ social media accounts, the actor gets into a heated argument with Evans, cementing her dislike of him.
Seyfried also re-creates Fielder’s meeting with Holmes in prison, since cameras are not allowed inside.
As the documentary comes to an end, Seyfried and Fielder question if Holmes is a victim or they, too, are being deceived.

“I still am not sure to this day what I experienced,” Fielder said during the Los Angeles screening. “It’s one of the reasons I’m excited for it to come out and more people to see it because it was just a small group for so long. I actually think maybe it being out there, everyone can help me understand what I went through.”

title: What the Victoria’s Secret CEO Calls the Store’s Customers, and Why
summary: Victoria’s Secret CEO Hillary Super explains why the company has a very specific way of referring to its customers.
story: Victoria’s Secret CEO Hillary Super says the company has a very specific way of referring to its customers.
“I would say, especially our younger customers want an in-store experience,” Super, who has served as Victoria’s Secret CEO since 2024, told Savannah Sellers in a story that aired Oct. 17 on TODAY.
“There is this tremendous opportunity to be a third space for her and a gathering place where she can come and shop and have fun with her friends.”
The wording caught Sellers’ ear.
“It’s interesting to me to hear you using ‘she’ and ‘her’ about your customer, like we’re talking about an individual that you know,” Sellers said.
“Yes,” replied Super.
“One of our brand values is to put her first,” Super continued. “Everything that we do, we do for her. We read all of the social comments. I read them every single night before I go to bed.”
The Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show will take place Oct. 18, live at 7:30 p.m. ET on YouTube. It’s the latest move for a company that is trying to regain trust with its customer base.

Known for making superstars out of the likes of Heidi Klum, Tyra Banks and Gisele Bündchen, Victoria’s Secret found itself making headlines when it came out that former owner Lex Wexner had close ties with Jeffrey Epstein.
Wexner resigned in 2020, while saying he didn’t do anything wrong and he wasn’t aware of Epstein’s criminal activity.

“It’s not something any of us really want to be tied to, but at the same time, it’s important to know, know that bit of history to understand how far we’ve come and how much we’ve changed,” Super told TODAY.
There have also been accusations about poor treatment of models, including harassment and assault related to the Epstein era. That environment also led to change.
“We have very strict protocols in our casting, in our fittings, in any model interaction, and it’s actually monitored by a designated individual. So we’ve come a long way in that regard,” said

There have also been changes to the way the brand recruits talent for the Victoria’s Secret and Pink brands. “We like the mix of OG angels, new talent, sports figures, influencers. It’s about the mix of the community,” Super said.
“We’re really thinking much more expansively about who an angel can be, and to me that’s about self-possession, and just personal confidence, strength, and feeling great in your own skin,” she added.

title: All About Elizabeth Holmes’ Prison Sentence: When She’s Out
summary: As the new Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” hits theaters, people are wondering when she will be out of prison.
story: As the buzzy new Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” hits theaters on Oct. 16, the former CEO of Theranos remains behind bars.
The film gives an unnerving and intimate look at Holmes’ life with partner Billy Evans and their two young children in the weeks leading up to the start of her federal prison sentence in May 2023.
Holmes, 42, was convicted in 2022 by a California jury of wire fraud after siphoning off hundreds of millions of dollars from several high-profile investors and misrepresenting Theranos technology.

The Silicon Valley startup had claimed that it was going to revolutionize healthcare with a machine that could conduct hundreds of medical tests on a single drop of blood. Prosecutors said that Holmes knew the technology was faulty and still solicited investors and business partners like Walgreens — something she denied during the trial.
In “You Can See Everything,” comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim spend extensive time with Holmes and her family.
A trailer released in September shows that Fielder moved into her house during the filming.
“I think this is the moment in time to capture this story before I’m gone,” she seemingly tells the comedian at one point.
Given Holmes’ backstory, Fielder asks her why she should be believed.
“That’s because I don’t have anything to hide,” she tells him.

News of “You Can See Everything” went viral after it was screened at the Telluride Film Festival in September, with attendees having strong reactions. Rebecca Keegan of NBC News Digital was among those in the crowd.
“There were audible gasps and ‘no ways’ consistently throughout this almost three-hour film,” she told NBC News correspondent Erin McLaughlin on TODAY Sept. 8.
The buzzy film also hits theaters three weeks after news broke that Holmes is expected to be moved from prison to a halfway house next year.
How Long Is Elizabeth Holmes’ Prison Sentence?
Holmes was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison in November 2022, but it has since been reduced.
In May 2023, U.S. District Judge Edward Davila ordered her to pay $452 million in restitution to the victims of her crimes.
Also, former Theranos president Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani was sentenced to nearly 13 years in prison and three years of probation after being convicted of 12 counts of fraud.
Holmes has been serving her sentence at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas.
When Will Elizabeth Holmes Be Released from Prison?

Her original prison sentence was reduced from 135 months to 123 months in March 2026 when a judge agreed she did not cause “substantial financial hardship” to her victims, according to a court document.
Her scheduled release date is now Feb. 22, 2030.
Holmes is also scheduled to be transferred from the minimum-security prison in Bryan to a halfway house in 2027, according to one of her victims. There has been no change in her release date.

Alan Eisenman, who invested about $1.2 million in Theranos, told NBC News on Sept. 24 that he was alerted by the Justice Department’s victim notification system that Holmes is to be transferred to the Austin Transitional Center. The halfway house is in an unincorporated community that borders Austin, Texas.

He said he has not received any money in restitution from Holmes that was part of the court ruling in 2023. Holmes’ attorney from her trial did not respond to a phone message from NBC News requesting comment.
Eisenman told NBC News he plans to watch “You Can See Everything.”
“She’s obviously manipulative,” Eisenman said. “If people don’t see that, then they’re blind. She’s the most conniving person I’ve ever met.”

title: Did the ‘Cheers’ Cast Drink Real Beer on the Show? George Wendt Revealed the Answer on TODAY in 1988
summary: “Cheers” star George Wendt spoke with TODAY in 1988 about whether he drinks beer on the show and what he hoped to do after the series ends.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment features “Cheers” star George Wendt on TODAY on Dec. 8, 1988, talking about the success of the show in the middle of its lengthy run.

“Cheers” remains one of the most beloved and critically acclaimed sitcoms in history, thanks in large part to a stellar cast that included George Wendt. The late actor played barfly Norm, the unmotivated accountant whose love of beer and the bar trumped everything else in his life.

Wendt, who died in 2025, would have turned 78 on Oct. 17. He earned six Emmy Award nominations for his portrayal of Norm, coming in six consecutive years from 1984 through 1989, the heart of the show’s 11-season run, from 1982 until 1993.
“Cheers” was a massive hit, so did Wendt feel any pressure to perform for a live audience?
“You get to like pressure after a while. If you don’t, you’re really in the wrong business because there’s so much of it,” he told Gene Shalit on TODAY on Dec. 8, 1988.
Did They Drink Beer on ‘Cheers’?
Norm’s greatest love was beer, so did Wendt actually drink real beer while shooting his scenes?
“It’s not beer. It’s ‘near beer,’ which I guess it’s not available in draft or in kegs, so they pour cans of ‘near beer’ into Coca-Cola dispensers and out it comes,” Wendt said.

“They do that before the audience gets in and it’s flat and warm and just horrible by the time we have to drink it,” he continued. “In the first couple of seasons, I used to just be swilling it, be a real actor, sort of behaving as a bar patron onstage. Now, I have a feel for where the cameras are, and I only drink it when I’m on camera.”
Would There Be a Letdown After He Finished ‘Cheers’?

“Cheers” rolled with the punches with cast turnover, including the death of Nicholas Colasanto, who played Coach, and Shelley Long’s decision to leave after the fifth season. Wendt said there would be a “huge letdown” when the show wrapped up, but he missed the mark in saying that the end of the comedy was on the horizon.

“I can get sentimental right away,” he said. “I mean, we had so many reasons to be sentimental, anyway. When Nick Colasanto died, when Shelley left, and now, you know, the imminent end of the show — not all that imminent — but the end is certainly closer than the beginning.”
“Cheers” would remain a ratings juggernaut until its series finale aired in May 1993.
“It’s kind of a sobering thought that Norm might be the best role I’ve ever had,” he said. “I mean, it’s definitely the best role I’ve ever had. Might be the best role I’ll ever have.”
When Was the Last Time George Wendt Had to Pay for a Beer?
Wendt may not have had real beer on the set, but he certainly was taken care of whenever he was out.
“I know, it’s one of the great perks of employment history. I get free beer wherever I go,” he said.
“Too bad you’re not in the series where you’re a Cadillac salesman,” Shalit said.

While the role of Norm afforded Wendt fame — and free beer — he also wanted to keep acting in any form once his time on the show ended, whether it was TV or film, something he would do for the duration of his career.

“We just want to do good work, if possible, and the medium isn’t really important. Let’s say stage, feature films and television. The more you can spread it around, it really stays interesting for you,” he said.

title: Who Is Billy Evans? Elizabeth Holmes’ Partner Seen in ‘You Can See Everything’ Documentary
summary: Elizabeth Holmes’ rise and fall as the disgraced founder of Theranos is the subject of the new A24 documentary “You Can See Everything,” which premieres in limited theaters on Oct. 16.
story: Elizabeth Holmes’ rise and fall as the disgraced founder of Theranos is the subject of the new A24 documentary “You Can See Everything,” which premieres in limited theaters on Oct. 16.
The documentary, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, goes behind the scenes to tell the story of how Holmes, 42, vowed to revolutionize blood testing only to end up a convicted felon.

After a 2022 federal investigation of Theranos labs uncovered critical violations, Holmes, who was just 19 when she founded the biotech company, was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud and sentenced to 11 years in prison.

“You Can See Everything” also delves into Holmes’ private life. The movie includes footage of Holmes with fiancé William “Billy” Evans and their two children that was shot in 2023 during her final days of freedom before she reported to a Texas federal prison.

According to the filmmakers, they revealed at a Los Angeles screening of the doc, Evans has yet to see the documentary. Fielder noted that after Holmes went to prison, Evans “started trying to exert a level of control over the process” that made it difficult to continue filming and “communication broke down.”

In February 2025, Holmes broke her silence to give her first prison interview to People. She described life behind bars, which includes two visits a week from Evans and their kids, as “hell and torture.”
“The people I love the most have to walk away as I stand here, a prisoner, and my reality sinks in,” Holmes said.
Read on to learn more about Holmes’ fiancé Evans.
Evans’ Grandparents Founded Several Luxury Hotels
In 1953, Evans’ grandparents, William and Anne Evans, founded Evans Hotels, a hospitality group consisting of several luxury hotels in San Diego, according to NPR.
Holmes and Evans Got Engaged in 2018, a Year After Meeting
Holmes met Evans at a charity event in Oct. 2017, she told People in her 2025 prison interview.
A year after meeting, Evans popped the question by presenting Holmes with a silver snake ring he bought at a Taylor Swift “Reputation” tour concert.
“I asked him 20 times if he wanted to spend his life with me,” Holmes said. “There were a million reasons why not.”
Evans Spoke of His Love for Holmes in a Pre-Trial Letter
Evans poured his heart out about Holmes in an emotional pre-trial letter to the judge in her case, reported The Independent.
In his 12-page letter, which also included photos of the couple, Evans wrote that he fell instantly in love with Holmes, whom he called “Liz.”
“I was captivated by her childish wonder and authenticity,” he wrote, adding “She listened more intently than anyone I had ever met.”
Evans praised Holmes’ vision, writing, “Her capacity to change the world is limitless.”
He also included the story of how Holmes competed in a Golden Gate Bridge ocean swim event in 2021 while pregnant with William.
“There were fifty reasons I thought it was a bad idea, the sharks, the tides, her complete inexperience swimming post age 14,” Evans wrote.
“You would think by now I would learn to not discount her perseverance,” he wrote.
Holmes and Evans Share 2 Kids
Holmes gave birth to the couple’s first child, son William, shortly before her fraud trial began.
She and Evans welcomed their second child, daughter Invicta, in 2023.
According to People, Holmes sat in the back seat of a Ford Expedition pumping breast milk for three-month-old Invicta as she approached the prison gates to begin her term.
Holmes ‘Always Wanted to Be a Mother’
While speaking to People, Holmes addressed speculation that she and Evans schemed to start a family to depict Holmes as more sympathetic so she might avoid time in prison.

“I know how the optics look, but I always wanted to be a mother,” Holmes said. “I truly did not think I would ever be convicted or found guilty. I kept talking to my lawyers and they also assured me we would never get this far.”
“It wasn’t planned and I can’t worry about what others think. It’s just when the timing happened,” Holmes added.

title: RJ Mitte’s Sister Pays Tribute To Late Actor: ‘I Not Only Just Lost A Brother, I Lost A Father’
summary: RJ Mitte’s sister Lacianne Carriere remembered the late actor as a strong support system who helped her during some of the family’s most difficult times.
story: RJ Mitte’s sister Lacianne Carriere remembered the late actor as a strong support system who helped her during some of the family’s most difficult times.

Carriere delivered a tearful, emotional speech, honoring Mitte at his celebration of life event on Oct. 16 in Brownsville, Texas, where he lived. It comes days after Mitte died by suicide, his representatives confirmed. He was 34.

In her speech, Carriere spoke about how Mitte ultimately became a father-figure to her during her earliest years, as their family navigated a devastating car accident that left their mother severely injured.

“R.J. Mitte was my older brother. But I not only just lost a brother, I lost my father,” Carriere told the crowd at Mitte Cultural District, an organization run by the family that hosted the event. “My mom was a single mother and when I was two weeks old, she was taken in an accident that paralyzed her from the waist down the first few years of my life, and my brother immediately took on the other role.”
Carriere added that “every part of me is R.J.”
“Every type of music I listen to, everything I watch, every game I play, our mannerisms — I just really miss my brother.”

The ceremony, which was live-streamed by the city of Brownsville, featured a number of speakers including his grandmother Anita Dianne Carriere, author M.J. Dougherty and publicist Nedda Soltani, many of whom shared sweet anecdotes about the “Breaking Bad” star.
Lacianne Carriere not only spoke about her connection to Mitte, but also her brother’s love for the city in which he lived.

“He loved Brownsville so much. He might not have been born or raised here, but this was his home,” she told the crowd. “This was his community. He loved it here, and he loved all of you, and he loved this city. And I want to thank you all for coming out.”
Carriere also shared a message for those who are struggling with their mental health.
“Please don’t feel like you’re alone. You’re never alone,” she said. “And just try, try to accept the help. Try, try your hardest, and just reach out to someone.
Carriere ended on an inside joke about her brother’s truck.
“And I want to say to R.J. I’m not going to sell that nasty truck,” she said, laughing. “It’s mine now. Thank you all so much for being here.”

Mitte died on Oct. 12, according to his obituary. His mother Dyna Carriere told NBC News that her son had no history of mental illness and never saw a therapist. However, she said that he had been going through a difficult emotional time recently. Still, he made no indication that he might end his life, she said.
“For the last three months, I’d been offering for him to go to therapy, trying to get him to go there, but he was like, ‘No, I’ve got it. It’s OK. I’m handling it,’” she told NBC News.

title: Carrie Preston Unpacks ‘Elsbeth’ Season 4, from Romantic Sparks with Smullen to the Arrival of Her Mom
summary: Carrie Preston tells TODAY.com what fans can expect from Season 4, including Elsbeth’s reunion with Kaya and a possible “will-they-won’t-they” romance with Smullen.
story: Elsbeth Tascioni has cracked some difficult cases over the years, but she’ll soon face one of her most challenging tasks yet: planning a wedding with her mother.

“Elsbeth” returned for its fourth season on Oct. 7 with an episode that hinted at where the whimsical consent decree lawyer’s storyline is headed. In “Crazy in Love,” Carrie Preston’s Elsbeth investigated a marriage counsellor named Serena Collyer, played by guest star Nicole Scherzinger, who murdered her secret lover.
To solve the case, Elsbeth worked with Detective Bobby Smullen (Danny Mastrogiorgio), who revealed he had recently separated from his wife.
Elsbeth and Smullen bickered about how to best handle the investigation and shared a brief moment where sparks seemed to fly between them.

While a new romance could be possible for Elsbeth this season, fans know for certain that one of the biggest plot points will be her involvement in son Teddy’s (Ben Levi Ross) wedding. She already seemed eager to help plan the nuptials in the series premiere, but the arrival of her mother could derail the happy occasion. When Teddy mentioned that his grandmother had been attempting to get in touch with his mom, Elsbeth’s usually cheerful disposition slightly dimmed.
Tony winner Christine Ebersole will play Elsbeth’s mother in Season 4, Variety reported, joining Uzo Aduba, Tyne Daly and more actors who are set to guest star.
Preston gushes that Ebersole is “incredible” in her role during an interview with TODAY.com.

“She really came in fully ready with the character, and we were like, ‘Oh, there’s mom. There she is! No rehearsal required.’ That’s the level of artistry that she brings to everything she does,” she praises.

The Emmy winner reveals that Elsbeth’s mom will add some tension to the lawyer’s personal and professional life, teasing that the premiere set the tone for the “complicated relationships” fans will see unfold.

Below, Preston opens up more about what fans can expect from Season 4, including Elsbeth’s reunion with Kaya (Carra Patterson) in the first half of the season, a possible “will-they-won’t-they” romance with Smullen and a current story dominating the news cycle that would make a great case.

It’s a dream to be able to even do a guest spot on a great show like “The Good Wife.” Then for that to have led to more appearances, and then to have led to appearances in a completely different show, and then to have a show centered around the character is very rare, and that rarity is not lost on me. The privilege is not lost on me. To be trusted with taking what was in essence a side dish and helping craft it into a main dish with incredible writers and an amazing showrunner like Jonathan Tolins and all of the incredible actors that I get to play with, has been really what I feel like I’ve been working for my whole life. So it means a great deal, which is an understatement. I’m also just excited every day that it’s something that people like yourself and audiences are enjoying and want to keep coming back for more because we’re having a great time doing it.

It’s been so fun to build her out as far as the people that she has relationships with. Because when we saw her as a guest star, she was the pinch hitter. She came in to hit the home run for the rest of that team. Now, she’s a detective. She was a lawyer before. We’ve seen her now on this show as a mother. Her son was mentioned one time in the entire universe of “The Good Wife” and “The Good Fight,” and now we’ve seen her as a girlfriend. This season we’re going to see her as a daughter. It’s fun to think about her in (relation) to other people. I’m excited to see where the writers are going to continue to take her as far as relationships, not just romantic ones.

That episode was so comedic and fun, and was also talking about relationships, setting up a season about complicated relationships. It’s definitely going to carry over as the season goes on. Teddy is getting married to Roy (Hayward Leach). Weddings, although they’re very joyous, sometimes bring families together in a way that can create some stress. It’s going to be fun to see what happens when Elsbeth’s mother comes, and we see a little bit more about the kind of upbringing that Elsbeth had, and the kind of mother that she was raised by, and parents. To learn about (why) Elsbeth wasn’t like the other kids growing up, and what that was like. Trying to fit in and all those things, which I think is going to just add more dimension and color to the character.

The thing that I love about our show is it’s not centered on a woman needing a man or feeling like a man completes her or she needs a man to make herself secure. Her primary relationship is with her work, and it’s with her son and her friends and reinventing herself at this age and stage in her life. That said, she’s someone who people are attracted to, and she is attracted to other people.

In the first episode, it was fun to play with the fact that sometimes you are attracted in a weird way to people that you are in opposition with. There’s sometimes a fine line between people who butt heads and people who kiss. Not that there’s anything going to happen with Smullen. I don’t know. I’m not in charge of the writing. But I do feel like it was a fun juxtaposition to what was happening with Nicole Scherzinger’s character in the episode. That’s just great writing, and I definitely trust our writers to take the character to places that I couldn’t even dream of.

There’s been a couple of times throughout the series where you see Elsbeth and Smullen connect in a way that is more personal. There are gentle little things where she’ll call him “Bobby.” When Bobby was so worried in the episode about the wigs that he wasn’t attractive, and so he got a wig himself, she said, “Bobby, you look great the way you are.” Just tender little things like that. I don’t think it’s a conscious thing on either of their parts. Just because you might have a kind or passing thought about someone doesn’t mean you’re going to act on it. But the will-they-won’t-they thing is what we were playing with in that first episode. I think the audience has definitely picked up on both of those things.

To the credit of our brilliant director of that episode, Nancy Hower — she’s the one who came to Danny Mastrogiorgio and I, and said, “Hey, why don’t we just go a little further for that moment? Let’s make it feel like, ‘Will they?’ at this moment.”

It turned into this tiny little thought, a little spark, a little something, which sometimes that’s the most delicious thing. The thing that you don’t act on. A little side note: Danny Mastrogiorgio and I went to Juilliard together, so we were classmates. I’ve known him for a very long time, so it was an interesting thing for us to play, and we certainly had a good time with it.

The writing, it’s all pretty centric around the wedding and the planning of the wedding, and what that does to Elsbeth when her mom’s around, when you’re self conscious about how you are in the world when you see yourself through your parents’ eyes. It’s hard sometimes not to feel like you’re somehow falling short.
